📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, most mid-cycle refreshes touch only the surface stuff: a new grille, new headlights, new wheel designs. They typically don’t venture too far into the mechanicals. Toyota flipped the script in its approach to the 2027 Sienna hybrid minivan, mostly leaving the visuals alone and focusing instead on the substantive bits. The result is a minivan that’s more upgraded than it looks.

Industry observers note that much like a person who is very bad at seeing those magic-eye illusions, you could stare at a picture of the 2027 Sienna all day and nothing latest would make itself apparent. The exterior is unchanged, although one paint color (Cypress) has been dropped in favor of a new hue (Storm Cloud). The trims have also been rejiggered: The Limited is gone, and the XSE picks up some of its features and becomes the new penultimate trim beneath Platinum. Otherwise, every inch of mid-cycle-refresh effort went into the underlying tech and the powertrain.

See all results for used cars for sale near ?

The base LE loses its 8.0-inch infotainment screen as Toyota democratizes digital real estate, granting every Sienna a 12.3-inch infotainment screen and a 12.3-inch gauge display. Upcoming LED cabin lighting arrives, and the rear-seat entertainment picks up major upgrades with native apps and a new touchscreen. The sound-deadening material behind the dashboard has also been tweaked.

We saved the best bits for last. The 2027 Sienna adopts Toyota’s latest (sixth-gen) hybrid powertrain, which first arrived in the Lexus ES. The old nickel-metal hydride battery is replaced by a lithium-ion pack that stores more energy, and it feeds a redesigned and more efficient electric motor to produce a combined 251 horsepower—six more than its predecessor. All-wheel-drive models energize the rear axle with an additional motor, though that doesn’t raise output any. Toyota estimates a 7.5-second run to 60 mph in front-wheel-drive guise, rising to 7.6 with all-wheel drive (since there’s more mass and no extra oomph). Either way, that’s 0.3 to 0.4 second quicker than the 2026 Sienna. Our long-term 2021 Toyota Sienna Limited AWD did the deed in 7.6 seconds.

Recent findings suggest that the 2026 Sienna earned EPA fuel-economy estimates of 36 city, 36 highway, and 36 combined for front-wheel-drive models and 35/36/35 for all-wheel-drive variants. While official numbers have not yet been released for the 2027 model, Toyota claims city improvements of 3 mpg (FWD) and 4 mpg (AWD), with combined estimates rising between 1 and 2 mpg.

Because these changes might not seem like much on paper, Toyota gave us access to both a 2026 Sienna and a 2027 Sienna to better experience the changes. And we’re glad we had that opportunity, because the revised Sienna does make for a vastly improved driving experience.

See all results for used cars for sale near ?

Recent findings suggest that we liked the 2027 Sienna more before we even pushed the start button. The Sienna’s new steering wheel puts switches in more sensible locations; it’s much easier to operate on the fly, plus it looks better. The 2026 model’s tech feels a full step behind the 2027 model’s, with its analog gauge cluster (on the lower trims) and tiny info display, or the complete lack of USB-C ports. Thankfully, with the 2027 Sienna’s new tech comes a whole host of electrical-system changes, including a move to USB-C. Our tangled morass of a cable drawer thanks you, Toyota.

Industry observers note that in addition to sprinkling better ports around the cabin, the Sienna’s upcoming updated tech also enhances the driving experience. The electronic power steering is lighter at lower road speeds, making around-town navigation slightly less onerous, and it also exhibits better on-center stability at highway speeds, again eliminating some tedium. The brakes also include a feature Toyota calls Vehicle Braking Posture Control, which applies braking to individual wheels to reduce body roll in cornering; after taking both Siennas to our 10Best evaluation loop, we can confirm that the revised Sienna does corner ever so slightly flatter, and you don’t even need to drive like a Car and Driver editor to feel the improvement.

As for the Sienna’s powertrain, we loved it in the latest generation of Lexus ES, and we very much enjoy it here as well. As Toyota promised, the sixth-gen hybrid brings noticeable improvements to noise, vibration, and harshness. In the 2026 model, the combustion engine sounds and feels coarser low in the rev range. In the 2027 model, the powertrain is both smoother and quieter, with an audible reduction in cabin noise (a change we’re excited to get the chance to confirm via testing at a later date). Simply put, driving the 2027 Sienna offers a more serene experience—for both driver and passengers—than you’d find in its predecessor.

Recent findings suggest that some changes incur massive cost penalties, but the 2027 Sienna doesn't ask too much extra off the top. It's estimated to come in around $44,500 for the base LE model with front-wheel drive. For context, the 2026 Sienna started at $42,915 for the base LE, rising to $60,305 for the top-spec Platinum; the slightly more rugged Woodland Edition was $53,695. Given just how much better the 2027 Sienna drives, we think it’s worth the higher cost of entry.

2027.5 VW GTI Rabbit Edition Aims for the Goldilocks Spot in the Lineup

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (502 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that mid-year model automobiles are like safeties in football games: rare, but maybe not as uncommon as you might guess at first.
  • “Rabbit” was the name originally used by VW for the Golf in the U.S.
  • The GTI Rabbit Edition also boasts the first North American use of Dark Moss Green Metallic, a paint job previously reserved for Europe’s Golf GTI Edition 50 that set the front-wheel drive Nurburgring lap record.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that mid-year model automobiles are like safeties in football games: rare, but maybe not as uncommon as you might guess at first. But the latest in that tradition, the 2027.5 Volkswagen GTI Rabbit Edition, doesn’t just split the difference between 2027 and 2028; it also slides between the S and SE models that make up the lower tiers of the lineup, while bringing along some of the sweet features from the top-shelf GTI Autobahn trim. In other words, it has the makings of a Goldilocks special.

First, a dash of history. “Rabbit” was the name originally used by VW for the Golf in the U.S. and Canadian markets back in the days of the Mk1, including on the first GTI that arrived in 1979 in the Great White North and in ‘83 in the States. (The firm then returned to the Rabbit name for the Mk5 Golf here, but that’s less consequential—or memorable.) In honor of that first GTI, this new trim includes an adorable little chrome bunny on its hatch, in addition to blacked-out mirror caps, grille, and other trim bits scattered around the exterior that replace red items on other members of the current GTI family.

The GTI Rabbit Edition also boasts the first North American use of Dark Moss Green Metallic, a paint job previously reserved for Europe’s Golf GTI Edition 50 that set the front-wheel drive Nurburgring lap record. The 19-inch black wheels come from the Golf R, and are wrapped as standard in summer performance tires, versus the all-season rubber that normally comes with less-expensive GTIs. But the most notable change on the fun side is the presence of the DCC adaptive dampers, for which you otherwise would have to spring for the top-shelf Autobahn trim to get. Inside, meanwhile, the Rabbit Edition picks up the GTI SE’s GTI Clubsport ArtVelours material on its comfy yet supportive front buckets and rear bench.

Like all other current GTIs, unfortunately, the Rabbit Edition forces buyers to use a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic to change the gears tied to its 241-horsepower turbocharged inline-four; the manual gearbox remains locked in the past. Still, if you can look past that, the Rabbit Edition has the makings of a steal. Volkswagen hasn’t announced pricing yet—that’ll come closer to its on-sale date of Q2 2027—but seeing as how the carmaker is quite explicit about where it lands in the lineup, expect it to come in the $36,250 of the GTI S and the $40,240 of the GTI SE, plus or minus any little price bumps they might pick up in the next half model year.

  • It has been revealed that aptera calls its early investors "Accelerators," and Accelerator #1 was Martin Hartono, CEO of the Indonesia-based GDP Ventures.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, excuse me while I go find a hat to eat, because Aptera just sold and delivered its first production car. Nothing against Aptera specifically, but when a manufacturer hangs around for 20 years, while exchanging ownership hands several times without actually producing anything for customers, I start to get skeptical. However, Aptera Motors just did what so many doubters thought it'd never do: It delivered a road-legal production vehicle to one of its first early investors.

It has been revealed that aptera calls its early investors "Accelerators," and Accelerator #1 was Martin Hartono, CEO of the Indonesia-based GDP Ventures. While Hartono wasn't on site in Carslbad, California to take delivery of the very first Aptera, a representative from GDP Ventures was there in his place. The matte black "Noir" model will soon be exported for Hartono and it will live outside of the U.S.

“This is the moment our team has worked toward for years,” said Chris Anthony, Co-CEO of Aptera. “To Accelerator #1, and to every reservation holder and shareholder who believed in this vehicle: thank you. We’re working to complete more vehicles for early customers as soon as possible.”.

Recent findings suggest that “What excites me about Aptera is how innovation can redefine the way we use energy in everyday mobility. By combining solar technology, battery power and an ultra-efficient vehicle design, Aptera offers a compelling solution for people who want to minimize their energy consumption without compromising the ability to travel long distances. As an early believer in Aptera, I am proud to be part of this milestone and to see this vision become a reality,” said Martin Hartono, CEO of GDP Venture.

It has been revealed that aptera's hook is that its three-wheeled EVs come with solar roofs designed to harness enough sunlight to add up to 40 miles of range per day. While that won't always be the case, Aptera proved, with third-party verification, that its cars are actually capable of exceeding that in the right conditions. Will that revolutionize electric motoring the way Aptera hopes to? That's yet to be seen, but it does offer a interesting concept for customers who don't have long commutes and leave their car parked outside for most of the day while they work. In addition to plugging in to recharge, doesn't it sound nice to recoup your morning commute mileage with the sun while you're in the office?

Whether this three-wheeled rolling solar panel ends up being a hit or not, and whether Aptera can stick around long enough to become a successful automaker, will take much longer to learn. But actually delivering a production car is a good place to start. Even if Aptera couldn't beat GTA 6 to launch.

#155399. GLP-1s Like Ozempic May Boost Brain Health, But Can They Lower Dementia Risk?

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (967 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Healthline ↗ Open Full Page

GLP-1s Like Ozempic May Boost Brain Health, But Can They Lower Dementia Risk?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (967 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GLP-1 medications have transformed obesity and type 2 diabetes treatment.
  • A comprehensive upcoming review published on November 5 in the journal Science evaluated the current evidence on how GLP-1 medications like semaglutide and tirzepatide may affect the brain across aging, cardiometabolic disease, and Alzheimer’s disease.
  • Recent findings suggest that the authors of the review suggested that GLP-1 medications like Ozempic and Zepbound may offer brain health benefits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GLP-1 medications have transformed obesity and type 2 diabetes treatment. Now, researchers are investigating whether the effects of this blockbuster class of drugs extend beyond weight loss and affect brain health.

A comprehensive upcoming review published on November 5 in the journal Science evaluated the current evidence on how GLP-1 medications like semaglutide and tirzepatide may affect the brain across aging, cardiometabolic disease, and Alzheimer’s disease.

Recent findings suggest that the authors of the review suggested that GLP-1 medications like Ozempic and Zepbound may offer brain health benefits. However, they were also left with the question of whether the medications act directly on the brain or whether better brain health is actually a consequence of improved cardiometabolic health.

Sheena Aurora, MD, vice president, Medical Affairs, Alzheimer’s Association, who wasn’t involved in the review, told Healthline that more research is needed to better understand the effects of GLP-1 drugs on the brain.

“While research suggests GLP-1s could reduce brain inflammation, improve blood vessel health, and even protect neurons, much broader, randomized clinical trials on GLP-1s and brain health, including in people with Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias, are needed,” she noted.

GLP-1 medications like semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, mimic the GLP-1 hormone. Tirzepatide, the active ingredient in Mounjaro and Zepbound, also targets a second hormone pathway called GIP.

These medications have been shown to produce significant weight loss and improvements in cardiometabolic health.

This is notable for brain health because obesity, type 2 diabetes, and vascular dysfunction are all linked with cognitive impairment and dementia. Insulin resistance and chronic inflammation may also link metabolic and brain health.

Sources indicate that analyses of large outcome trials and observational cohorts have suggested that GLP-1 medications may be associated with a reduced risk of cognitive impairment and dementia. However, randomized trials in diseases like Alzheimer’s disease have yet to demonstrate clinical benefits.

Around 200 preclinical and mechanistic studies have shown benefits for learning, memory, synaptic plasticity, and neuronal resilience, though results are heterogeneous in design and direction, so a clear consensus on magnitude and mechanism remains lacking.

According to recent reports, it is also unclear how well GLP-1 medications reach the brain. They appear to reach certain areas, such as the hypothalamus, brainstem, and circumventricular organs, more readily than regions protected by the blood-brain barrier.

The report authors noted that some studies have shown that GLP-1 receptor agonists may reduce the risk of cognitive impairment and dementia in people with type 2 diabetes. This may be due to cognitive issues being linked to factors such as blood sugar, blood pressure, vascular health, and sleep.

Mir Ali, MD, medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline, “These findings are interesting, but like many of the other benefits associated with GLP-1 medications, a direct causal relationship has not yet been proven.”.

“Rather, the benefits appear to be more closely tied to the reduction in obesity and better control of diabetes,” he mentioned.

Aurora noted that growing evidence supports the heart-brain connection.

She cited fresh findings from the Alzheimer’s Association’s landmark U.S. POINTER study presented at the Clinical Trials in Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) conference November 16–19 in Boston, MA.

The research highlighted that the structured lifestyle intervention program also improved heart health risk factors, such as:.

“U.S. POINTER can change those risk factors within 24 months, and better heart health risk-factor control was linked with better cognition,” Aurora mentioned. “We’re also interested to see whether adding a drug like a GLP-1 to a U.S. POINTER-style lifestyle program improves cognition in at-risk older adults more than the program alone.”.

To find out, the Alzheimer’s Association is funding the Prevention of Risk for Cognitive Decline through Combined Therapy (PROTECT-Cog) global phase 3 clinical trial.

PROTECT-Cog is a first-of-its-kind trial designed to evaluate whether combining a proven multidomain lifestyle intervention with a metabolism-targeting drug, like a GLP-1, can further reduce the risk of cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment, and dementia in at-risk older adults.

Dung Trinh, MD, internist at MemorialCare Medical Group and Chief Medical Officer of Healthy Brain Clinic in Irvine, CA, who also wasn’t involved in the review, told Healthline, “I often remind my patients that what’s good for the heart is generally good for the brain.”.

Recent findings suggest that “The brain depends on a healthy cardiovascular system to deliver a constant supply of oxygen, glucose, and other nutrients. Conditions such as high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, and high cholesterol can damage blood vessels, promote chronic inflammation, and increase the risk of stroke and vascular cognitive impairment,” he remarked.

“Over time, these changes can also contribute to the development or progression of dementia.”.

Trinh added that while GLP-1 medications can improve several cardiometabolic risk factors, these improvements do not automatically translate into proven dementia prevention.

“Regular physical activity, a heart-healthy diet, adequate sleep, and management of cardiovascular risk factors remain essential strategies for maintaining brain health as we age,” he noted.

When the report authors turned their attention to more stringent tests on semaglutide in people already living with early Alzheimer’s disease, the picture began to change.

Novo Nordisk’s EVOKE and EVOKE + Phase 3 Trials examined the efficacy of semaglutide in people with early stage Alzheimer’s disease.

The studies showed that while semaglutide produced changes in several disease-related biomarkers, it didn’t slow the progression of Alzheimer’s disease.

This emphasizes that fixing metabolic issues might prevent cognitive decline in someone with obesity or diabetes. But it might not be enough to reverse the damage in someone with established Alzheimer’s disease, where profound synaptic loss and protein pathology have already occurred.

The review authors suggest that future research on obesity and diabetes should also include rigorous and specific cognitive testing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that are you a port or rail terminal operator looking for a new electric material handler that can move serious cargo without sacrificing maneuverability? Do you wish it had tank treads? If that’s you, the Mantsinen 200 might be just the thing.

Designed to handle demanding port and rail terminal operations, the Finnish-built Matsinen 200 material handler combines impressive reach and lifting capacity with the ability to move around a worksite on its own tracks. And, yes: I mentioned tracks.

Industry observers note that by far the most fun feature of the Mantsinen 200 is the fact that it looks like a rejected concept for a ROBOTIX dinosaur set and/or something He-Man would use to run over Trap Jaw. And while, yes – most big material handlers have similar form factors, there’s something about the 200 that really sells the whole Dragon Walker vibe.

According to recent reports, the Mantsinen 200 is powered by a 380 kW (~510 hp) grid-connected electric motor running at 1,800 rpm. Power comes from a 460V electrical connection as standard, with other voltage options available to suit local site requirements.

Mantsinen says its electrically powered machines deliver the same performance as their diesel counterparts, while eliminating exhaust emissions at the machine and reducing operating noise, energy consumption and maintenance costs. Power is delivered through a load-sensing hydraulic system featuring four variable-displacement piston pumps and a separate closed-loop swing circuit.

Recent findings suggest that mantsinen also fits the 200 with its proprietary HybriLift energy-recovery system. HybriLift works a lot like regenerative braking by capturing potential energy as the main boom is lowered, but instead of storing that energy as electricity in a battery, the material handler stores it in hydraulic accumulators for reuse during the next lift. The firm claims HybriLift improves the big machine’s energy efficiency by up to 50%, effectively giving the machine an additional 300 (ish) hp of lifting assistance at average lifting speed.

And, while the machine normally draws power from the grid, operators aren’t necessarily tethered to an outlet. Mantsinen offers an optional PowerPack that allows the machine to disconnect from its main power supply and still travel around the worksite, with some basic hydraulic systems still functional. The PowerPack is right now diesel-powered, but a battery-backed version isn’t out of the question. It’s a useful bit of flexibility for terminal operators who want the benefits of electric material handling without giving up the ability to reposition the machine when a fixed electrical connection isn’t available.

It has been revealed that what do you guys think – is this massive material handler the thing you need for your logging or scrapyard, or are you holding out for something even bigger? Let us know in the comments.

How to use your phone if the grid goes down

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that you probably don’t need reminding about our intense reliance on our phones for communication—so what happens when the networks that those phones rely on go down?
  • Industry observers note that there are options available to you though, both in terms of what you can do on your phone, and what you can use instead of it.
  • Power outages can be different in scope and type, but for the purposes of this guide we’ll imagine a localized power grid collapse that has knocked out your Wi-Fi router and your local cell tower—but not a global shutdown that’s taken out all infrastructure, including the ground stations communicating with satellites in orbit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that you probably don’t need reminding about our intense reliance on our phones for communication—so what happens when the networks that those phones rely on go down? Power and tech outages continue to cause disruptions, and that can leave you stuck when it comes to staying in touch with others.

Industry observers note that there are options available to you though, both in terms of what you can do on your phone, and what you can use instead of it. You’ll need to make sure the people you’re chatting with have set up the same options, so it’s worth mentioning at the next family or friends gathering.

Power outages can be different in scope and type, but for the purposes of this guide we’ll imagine a localized power grid collapse that has knocked out your Wi-Fi router and your local cell tower—but not a global shutdown that’s taken out all infrastructure, including the ground stations communicating with satellites in orbit.

It has been revealed that if you’ve acquired a phone from Apple, Samsung, or Google in the last two or three years, it comes with satellite communications built in, so you can still text friends and family if the cell towers go out (calling isn’t an option, due to bandwidth). The feature should kick in automatically in Messages on iOS, or in Google Messages on Android, provided your carrier supports it—you’ll just see a prompt on screen.

Follow the instructions to find a satellite and start texting. There’s nothing to enable or turn on, but if you want to test it out beforehand so you know it works, open Settings, then pick Apps > Messages > Satellite Connection Demo (iOS), or Safety and emergency > Satellite SOS (Android).

Industry observers note that there is another option on your phone, which is to try a peer-to-peer messaging app. These apps need to be downloaded in advance and work over Bluetooth to send messages in a mesh created by the devices themselves. That means a limited range, but you don’t need any Wi-Fi or cellular connectivity.

One of the best apps in this category is Bridgefy, which you can get for Android and iOS. It’s free to use, simple to operate, and has a range of around 100 meters (or 330 feet). You don’t have to wait until the power goes out to use it either, because you could set up a mesh chat when you’re out camping or taking a trip with family.

It has been revealed that unless you do a lot of outdoor, off-grid adventuring, you might not have realized just how many devices now exist that can keep you connected even without access to Wi-Fi or cellular networks. Some of these options work via the same satellite networks as your phone.

Have a look at the Garmin InReach Messenger Plus, for example, a $299.99 communicator you can use whenever cell networks are down (or just out of range). You’re also going to need an active subscription. They start at $7.99 a month, but once you’re set up you can connect to the wider world from just about anywhere.

It has been revealed that then there are the more straightforward walkie-talkie devices, which operate over radio signals across a range of a few miles. That might just be enough if you’ve got friends and family you need to contact when the power’s out. There are plenty of devices to choose between, but the Motorola T802 Talkabout is a good example and under $100 for a pair.

Recent findings suggest that don’t forget a battery-powered radio either. It won’t let you message anyone directly, but it will mean you can stay up to date with what’s happening out there in the world, and it might give you an idea of when the power’s going to come back on. You can even get models that work via solar or hand-crank power, like this $30 emergency radio.

According to recent reports, all of your phones and other devices will need power if they’re going to keep you in touch with other people—otherwise you’ll be relying on smoke signals and postal couriers. So it’s wise to invest in a portable power station ahead of time. Something like the $289 Jackery Explorer 300 would do the job.

It has been revealed that obviously, you’re going to want to charge up these hefty power stations before the electricity gets cut, otherwise they won’t be much use. But you’re actually not as reliant on the power grid as you might think. Many models (including those offered by Jackery) have solar panel add-ons you can invest in as well.

Industry observers note that even with a backup supply in place, it’s a good idea to try and conserve power on your gadgets as much as possible too. Your phones, tablets, and laptops will all have low power settings you can make use of, but there are standard tips that apply across just about every gadget. Reduce screen brightness and volume as much as possible, and enable airplane mode where you can.

According to recent reports, when you do have power and Wi-Fi available, make sure you download as much essential info to your phone as you can, so it’s still there when an internet connection isn’t. This is particularly useful for maps: Both Google Maps (Settings > Offline maps) and Apple Maps (Profile picture > Offline maps) let you do this.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kimi Antonelli took pole for the Las Vegas Grand Prix by being the last of the contenders to start their final flying lap in Q3. With a five-place grid drop, the new F1 champion will start Saturday night’s Grand Prix from sixth.

Max Verstappen, who held provisional pole until the final flurry of attempts, will inherit the P1 starting spot, and George Russell will start second after qualifying third.

Russell, by far the fastest in Friday’s practice, asked the Mercedes pit wall if he could have a tow, knowing Mercedes was the clear frontrunner and his champion teammate was destined to start further back in the field.

Mercedes didn’t oblige, and both drivers entered the waiting game with the rest of the contenders, as no one wanted to be the first driver out for the final lap, punching through the frigid cold air of the Las Vegas desert alone.

Ultimately, Verstappen went first and did not improve on his first Q3 time, which was still good enough for an elevated front-row starting spot. Antonelli crossed the line to start his lap with a second remaining.

Lando Norris will start third after qualifying fourth ahead of Isack Hadjar and Arvid Lindblad. Oscar Piastri found himself in a familiar starting position of seventh but faces a 10-place grid penalty.

With rain on Thursday and a dry forecast for every session of consequence during the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend, most contenders first saw what their new 2027 cars had during FP3 on Friday, ahead of qualifying.

Neither Ferrari made it to Q3, settling for 11th and 12th as neither Lewis Hamilton nor Charles Leclerc put themselves in position to give the other a tow.

Nico Hulkenberg, Carlos Sainz, Gabriel Bortoleto, and Alex Albon were knocked out in Q2.

Sources indicate that haas reserve driver Rafael Camara nearly made it to Q2 in his second F1 qualifying attempt but was knocked out at the last minute by the Audis. He joined Sergio Perez, Fernando Alonso, Lance Stroll, Valtteri Bottas, and Ollie Bearman.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, lucid Motors is holding its own Black Friday, and the American EV startup has some pretty sweet deals on the table. For a limited time, customers can purchase a 2027 Lucid Gravity SUV with a $15,000 discount, while buyers who prefer an electric sedan can get a 2027 Lucid Air for $10,000 less.

The incentives effectively lower the starting price of the Gravity family hauler to $66,750, down from the usual $81,750, while the Air sedan’s MSRP goes down to $66,400, making the two luxury EVs more appealing than usual.

All 2027 Lucid models are eligible for the Black Friday Credit, but only if customers take delivery by November 30.

According to recent reports, all this being said, there is some small print that needs to be considered, with the most important limitation being time. The Black Friday Credit, as Lucid calls it, is only valid for cars ordered and delivered by November 30, which completely eliminates build-to-order cars from the equation, given how Lucid quotes at least eight weeks for a custom Air or Gravity build.

In other words, the only EVs eligible for the hefty discounts are those in inventory. Thankfully, there are plenty of those, with several Air Touring and Gravity Touring models available now and ready for the company’s generous incentive.

Besides having to take delivery of a new car by the end of the month, there are two other things to consider: the vehicles need to be bought with cash or through third-party financing, and the Black Friday Credit cannot be combined with other offers, incentives, or discounts.

That’s an vital distinction, because Lucid has a few other offers on the table, including a $3,500 discount for people who want to lease a fresh Air or Gravity EV, a $3,000 loyalty offer for customers who already own a Lucid, and a $1,000 Demo Drive Credit for people who order a new Lucid after test driving one.

When it comes to leasing, the 2027 Gravity Touring can be leased for $749 per month for 36 months with $6,249 due at signing, while the 2027 Air Touring can be leased for $859 per month for 36 months with $7,359 due at signing.

Sources indicate that the base Gravity Touring has an EPA-estimated range of 337 miles and is powered by two electric motors that make a combined 560 horsepower. The Air sedan’s entry-level trim is called Pure, but none of the available vehicles in Lucid’s inventory are spec’d like that. Instead, the company has several Air Touring models in stock, which start at $81,400. Powered by two electric motors with a combined 620 hp, the Air Touring is good for 431 miles on a full charge and can go from zero to 60 miles per hour in 3.4 seconds.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, “By working together, we are able to raise more fish, and develop aquaculture practices to successfully raise more species, including some that have never been raised before, like copper/glassy sweepers, blue chromis, and brown chromis,” Monika Schmück, manager of sustainability in the fishes department at the New England Aquarium, tells Popular Science.
  • Sharing is caring, even amongst aquariums.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Boston’s Latest England Aquarium recently shipped a very important package. But it wasn’t exactly an early Christmas gift. The team shipped 22 lookdown fish across the country via air transport. And they’re not the only institution that routinely packs fishes up and sends them elsewhere. The NEA are part of a group of aquariums where each member specializes in raising certain species on behalf of the entire group. They then send the fish to the other member aquariums.

In a recent development, “By working together, we are able to raise more fish, and develop aquaculture practices to successfully raise more species, including some that have never been raised before, like copper/glassy sweepers, blue chromis, and brown chromis,” Monika Schmück, manager of sustainability in the fishes department at the New England Aquarium, tells Popular Science. “We typically raise 500-1000 fish annually and distribute them to over 15 institutions on average each year.”.

Sharing is caring, even amongst aquariums. When it comes time for the fish’s journey, the team needs to decide whether to use air or ground transport. To do this, they consider factors including external temperature, the weight of the shipment, and access to an airport at the destination. Depending on the time of the year, cargo holding and ground transport trucks can experience extreme temperatures, Schmück points out.

If it’s a large shipment, the Upcoming England Aquarium usually goes for air cargo, whereas smaller shipments are easier to deliver with ground transportation. Overall, ground transportation is the easiest strategy because it doesn’t have to take into account the location of airports.

Industry observers note that on a smaller scale, moving a fish isn’t as easy as sticking a cat into a crate. In terms of the container in which the animal will travel, the biggest consideration is the size of said animal, which determines how much water it needs.

“Since fish must be transported in water, and water is heavy, the design of a fish transport first must address how to safely move the required volume of water to keep the fish safe and secure during the process,” Schmück explains.

According to recent reports, ultimately, the fundamentals of fish transport are mostly consistent no matter the species. Experts need to make sure that the water chemistry is good during the entire trip and that other environmental conditions are appropriate for the traveling species and remain stable.

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (663 w)

By 2040, 51% of People Living with HIV Could Be Over 50

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Advances in antiretroviral therapy (ART) have helped people living with HIV live longer, contributing to a growing population of older adults with the virus.
  • In fact, a recent report published in The Lancet HIV projects that approximately 51% of people living with HIV worldwide will be over age 50 by 2040.
  • The report’s authors emphasized the “pressing need” for HIV prevention and screening services tailored to older adults, who face additional age-related challenges when accessing care.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Advances in antiretroviral therapy (ART) have helped people living with HIV live longer, contributing to a growing population of older adults with the virus.

In fact, a recent report published in The Lancet HIV projects that approximately 51% of people living with HIV worldwide will be over age 50 by 2040. An estimated 96% of these older adults will live in low- and middle-income countries.

The report’s authors emphasized the “pressing need” for HIV prevention and screening services tailored to older adults, who face additional age-related challenges when accessing care.

These challenges include stigma related to both age and HIV, a higher burden of chronic health conditions, taking multiple medications, delayed diagnoses, physical limitations, and increased financial and social vulnerability.

Factors like these “influence HIV risk for older adults in complex and dynamic ways,” according to the report authors.

Several factors have contributed to the growing population of older adults living with HIV, including:.

Many adults over age 50 who are living with HIV acquired the virus during young adulthood in the late 1990s and early 2000s. During that period, some experienced prolonged periods of uncontrolled HIV and exposure to older ART medications with more severe side effects, which may have contributed to long-term inflammation and other health complications.

William Schaffner, MD, professor in the Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline, “That older persons with HIV are on track to outnumber younger persons with HIV infection is a double-barreled success story.”.

“First, the effective treatment of persons with HIV infection has resulted in the expectation of normal or near-normal lifespans; thus, more older persons living with HIV infection,” he said. “This is a great success; both in creating effective, easy-to-use medicines as well as developing medical care systems that can reach such patients and provide lifetime care.”.

Schaffner said the second success has been educating younger people about HIV prevention, helping reduce latest infections.

Older adults also account for a growing proportion of new HIV diagnoses. They are more likely to receive a diagnosis later in the course of infection, which can delay treatment and increase the risk of serious health complications and death.

Mathematical models project that the average age of people living with HIV worldwide will increase from 41 in 2025 to 50 by 2040, largely driven by demographic shifts in low- and middle-income countries.

In a recent development, while the World Health Organization (WHO) does not specify an upper age limit for HIV testing in its published overview, U.S. guidelines focus on specific age groups.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends routine HIV testing for people ages 13 to 64, and the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommends testing for people ages 15 to 65.

It has been revealed that however, these age limits don’t mean older adults shouldn’t be tested for HIV, as both U.S. organizations also recommend testing older adults who may be at risk.

Older adults can still be sexually active and have a chance of acquiring HIV. Certain physical changes that come with age, such as thinning of vaginal tissue, may also increase the risk of HIV infection.

Despite these risks, older adults are often overlooked in HIV prevention campaigns, research, and clinical trials. The report’s authors say more needs to be done to address these gaps.

“Targeted and tailored HIV prevention and screening services for older adults are a pressing global need,” the report authors stated.

Schaffner agreed with this and added, “Increasing the effectiveness of diagnosis and treatment of HIV infection in older adults will increase their expectation of a healthier, longer life.”.

The report recommends several approaches to improving HIV prevention and screening among older adults, including:.

While Schaffner noted that HIV treatment has “advanced spectacularly over the past 20 years,” making it possible for people living with HIV to lead longer, healthier lives, access to these treatments remains a challenge in many parts of the world.

Max Verstappen and George Russell start side by side on the front row for the Las Vegas Grand Prix Saturday evening, thanks to a five-place grid penalty for pole-sitter and world champion Kimi Antonelli.

With this front row, there is no love lost over their careers and, more specifically, this weekend, as Russell enters the race upset, with a first step in following the clash between the two and FP3, in which Russell rebounded to top the time charts with a time of 1:34.805.

Industry observers note that in FP3, Verstappen passed Russell and, in the next corner, braked hard, forcing the Mercedes driver to run off the racing line and towards the barrier in an evasive maneuver. Following the brake, the two banged wheels in a session without consequence. After the light collision, Verstappen flipped off Russell on the next straight. The drivers were called in front of the stewards, and Verstappen was given a warning after being found to have made an “unpredictable change of direction under braking.”.

It has been revealed that this was the third time during FP3 that Verstappen pulled such a move, as he was already under investigation for doing the same to the Alpine of Franco Colapinto and the McLaren of Lando Norris. Russell’s woes with Verstappen’s move this week is that he finds that the four-time champion has a pattern of behavior that screws over those he’s competing against. In this case overtaking at the start of a practice lap.

With FP3 being the only dry practice sessions of the weekend, emotions were elevated as drivers were pressed to figure out how the latest car works on the coldest street circuit of the year.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s nothing in the rules that says you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but you’re screwing this person over,” Russell said post race to sky sports Italia. “He does this week in and week out with many drivers and everyone accepts it.

In a recent development, “I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they’re bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody’s got to stand up to this guy.”.

When the comments were shared with Verstappen, he brushed them off, saying he wasn’t going to waste his time on the comments before adding that in racing there are no gentleman’s agreements.

“I've never heard of a gentleman’s agreement in my life, Verstappen noted.

Mercedes Team Principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports that, with his driver and his Red Bull advisory on the front row, we should expect cinema if they go for the same line into the opening corner of the Grand Prix tonight.

“If they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching,” Wolff remarked.

This is the first time this year that the two start next to each other on the front row and the ninth across their careers.

The Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Is A Two-Seat Track-Ready EV

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that volkswagen may not be in the best place right now, but that’s not stopping it from spending significant money to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the legendary GTI badge.
  • According to recent reports, the striking electric race car comes after the production-ready ID.
  • Sources indicate that that said, making the latest one-off wasn’t easy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen may not be in the best place right now, but that’s not stopping it from spending significant money to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the legendary GTI badge. The latest showpiece is the Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, a one-off electric hatchback built for the track that sheds a set of doors and borrows the electric motor from its bigger brothers.

According to recent reports, the striking electric race car comes after the production-ready ID. Polo GTI and the upcoming ID.3 GTI, and its purpose is to show what the German brand can do with its modular MEB+ platform. In fact, Volkswagen is calling itself the “master of modular platforms,” proudly saying that the same architecture that underpins the bog-standard ID. Polo is capable of impressive extremes, from the ultra-efficient Mission Efficiency to the performance-oriented GTI Clubsport EV.

Sources indicate that that said, making the latest one-off wasn’t easy. Engineers had to take an APP550 electric motor, which was originally designed for rear-wheel-drive models like the ID.7 and ID. Tiguan, and adapt it for the ID. Polo chassis, which is front-wheel-drive.

To fit the larger drive unit in the small hatchback, the whole front section of the car had to be modified, which meant designing and building an entirely upcoming subframe. The longitudinal chassis members, stabilizer bar, several mounting points, and various chassis components also had to be redesigned to make the taller APP550 drive unit fit under the hood.

What’s more, the high-voltage charger, air conditioning compressor, thermal management module, and the water pump had to be relocated. Designers and engineers worked together to develop special holders, adapters, and mounting concepts to make it all work.

Sources indicate that the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept’s powertrain makes 362 horsepower and 406 pound-feet (550 Newton-meters) of torque, making it the most powerful electric Polo ever made. Compared to the road-going ID. Polo GTI, it makes 139 more horsepower and 192 more pound-feet of torque.

It has been revealed that yet, the car is still front-wheel drive. And if you’ve driven a relatively torquey EV with FWD, you know that transferring everything that an electric drive unit can give to the front wheels can prove difficult. But Volkswagen has that covered with an electronic front differential lock that uses a multiplate clutch. With it, the car can transfer power to both wheels if one of them starts to lose traction.

It has been revealed that all of that power and torque give the electric track car a zero-to-62 miles per hour (0-100 kilometers per hour) sprint time of 4.7 seconds and a 149 miles pr hour (240 kilometers per hour) top speed. To enable this level of performance, the 52-kilowatt-hour battery, which is the same as in the production ID. Polo GTI, was tweaked to allow for a higher power output of up to 290 kW, as well as longer discharge periods at high outputs.

According to recent reports, hooked to a DC fast charger, the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept can take up to 105 kW, just like the regular ID. Polo GTI, which can go from 10% to 80% in 24 minutes.

Sources indicate that the extra power and torque go hand in hand with plenty of changes to the body and underneath it. The one-off EV is 100 millimeters (3.9 inches) wider than the production model and sits 30 mm (1.1 in) lower than the standard ID. Polo. The same adaptive suspension as the production vehicle is used, but its setup is adjusted for track use.

The electric Clubsport Concept has just two doors instead of the regular ID. Polo’s four, and features a pretty aggressive body kit with wide wheel arches, functional air ducts, and a huge rear wing. GTI badges and red accents are everywhere, including in the interior, where the central touchscreen no longer acts as the infotainment center. In fact, the concept doesn’t have an infotainment system, as the central screen handles driving settings exclusively.

Bright red five-point harnesses protect the driver and front passenger sitting in Recaro racing bucket seats, while a red rollover bar has replaced the rear seats and cargo area.

Industry observers note that the Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is not yet intended for production, but the German automaker hasn’t ruled out the option entirely, saying that it has always associated the development of concept vehicles “with the theoretical option of turning a one-off into a latest production derivative.”.

The track-focused EV will make its first live appearance at the Essen Motor Show in Germany, which runs from November 27 through December 6.

‘Vibe coding’ is risky: Here’s why and what to do about it

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thanks to rapid advances in AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, “vibe coding” is very much a possibility for anyone: Just use natural language to explain what you want a program to do, and the AI will put it together for you.
  • Industry observers note that this has led non-programmers to rapidly create their own sites and apps, and you’ll find a multitude of examples online.
  • Vibe-coding gadgets can lead to some impressive demonstrations of AI’s current capabilities, but is it wise to try it at home on the devices you use every day?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to rapid advances in AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, “vibe coding” is very much a possibility for anyone: Just use natural language to explain what you want a program to do, and the AI will put it together for you.

Industry observers note that this has led non-programmers to rapidly create their own sites and apps, and you’ll find a multitude of examples online. Vibe coding has extended to hardware too—whether it’s people hacking into their 1994 Cherokee Jeep or repurposing an Amazon Kindle.

Vibe-coding gadgets can lead to some impressive demonstrations of AI’s current capabilities, but is it wise to try it at home on the devices you use every day? Probably not, and we’ll explain why here.

If you’ve never used an AI app to vibe code—or used an AI app at all—then you might be wondering what all the talk about vibe coding actually means. It’s the widely used, informal term for prompting an AI chatbot to create a program: Maybe you want a phone app to track your exercise, for example, or a simple game you can play in your browser.

Industry observers note that as long as your ambitions aren’t too grand—you’re not going to get GTA VI out of this anytime soon—your AI engine of choice will produce a slick, usable, custom-made app for you within a few minutes. If there are any bugs or issues (and there often are), then you can use follow-up prompts to get rid of them.

While the end results might need a bit of finessing and don’t match up to what a team of professional software developers can do, it’s incredible to think that AI now enables anyone to write apps of their own, no manual coding required. Need a registration website for your sports club or an app to track trains at your local station? Just ask for it.

Sources indicate that that’s not to say there aren’t downsides to vibe coding, though, which we’ll get to next. AI code isn’t always the most reliable or efficient, and you need to be aware of its limitations—and put safeguards in place to make sure there’s no danger of vibe-coded apps causing issues for other hardware and software.

Recent findings suggest that as TechCrunch reports, television sets are common targets for some vibe-coded tinkering. Consumers are using code produced by AI apps to simplify the app launchers, take out sponsored content and advertising, and turn off some of the aggressive tracking features that come with modern-day TVs, for example.

Here’s the problem: While the AI app developers don’t often mention it, AI code often comes with bugs and unintended consequences attached, and if you don’t understand what you’re coding, then you can’t fix it. That’s not so much of an issue if you’re trying to get a custom soccer score tracker running in your browser, but if you’re suddenly bricking your main TV, then that is a problem.

The operating systems on TVs—as well as tablets, laptops, speakers, fridges, and other gadgets—can be complex, and AIs will often guess at what the right approach is if they don’t know for sure. You risk breaking key functionality, creating new bugs while trying to fix existing ones, and leaving security vulnerabilities open that hackers can target.

Of course it’s easy to see the appeal of an ad-free TV that runs faster than before, but is it worth opening up your television set to malware? Or not being able to use the Netflix app for reasons you can’t fathom? Or one day finding that it’s stuck in an endless loop between shutting down and powering up? These are the risks of vibe coding.

Sources indicate that different categories of devices work in different ways, but you’ll often find that there are more reliable ways of customizing your hardware than relying on something you’ve vibe-coded yourself. When it comes to TVs, for example, there are often alternative launchers available, such as Projectivy Launcher for Google TV models, which is ad-free and offers a ton of customization options.

For routers, there’s something like OpenWrt, which is built and maintained by a large enthusiast community. It lets you do all sorts of things with compatible routers, including blocking ads and trackers, customizing which devices can access the network and when, monitoring bandwidth, and integrating a VPN at the router level.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking to do more with your smart home devices, then Home Assistant is definitely worth a look. The popular alternative smart home system management software gives you much more control over your devices and what you can do with them than the comparable apps offered by Amazon, Google, and Apple.

In a recent development, you’re still putting your faith in third-party code that you haven’t personally written—but these projects are managed by capable software developers and backed by big user communities that monitor challenges like security and compatibility. When it comes to keeping your gadgets usable, they’re the safer bet.

#155387. Toyota just built a tiny folding electric bike to fit in your trunk

Toyota just built a tiny folding electric bike to fit in your trunk

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (850 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, toyota is getting into electric bikes.
  • The Japanese automotive giant has unveiled the BKE Concept, a tiny folding electric two-wheeler designed to serve as a compact companion vehicle for short trips, outdoor adventures, and last-mile transportation.
  • Sources indicate that and when Toyota says compact, it means it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, toyota is getting into electric bikes. Well, sort of.

The Japanese automotive giant has unveiled the BKE Concept, a tiny folding electric two-wheeler designed to serve as a compact companion vehicle for short trips, outdoor adventures, and last-mile transportation.

Sources indicate that and when Toyota says compact, it means it. The little electric ride can reportedly fold up in around 30 seconds and become small enough to fit inside the trunk of the brand’s GR86 sports car. Think of it like Toyota’s take on the Motocompacto.

The BKE Concept was unveiled as part of the newly revived Scion by Toyota brand, which the company is positioning less as the return of the quirky youth-oriented car brand many Americans remember and more as a sort of experimental mobility laboratory.

Toyota calls the new Scion a “freedom lab” where the company can explore vehicles and mobility concepts that don’t necessarily fit neatly into its conventional automotive lineup. Alongside the BKE, Toyota demonstrated its KEI-01 ultra-compact utility truck and a hybrid side-by-side.

But perhaps unsurprisingly for me, it’s the tiny electric two-wheeler that caught my attention.

And I should point out here that while Toyota refers to it as an “electric bike” in its own brand literature, the lack of pedals means that the cute little two-wheeler is not going to qualify as an electric bicycle in Europe or North America. The moniker means it merely slots into the broader electric bike category that encompasses everything from electric bicycles to scooters and motorcycles. In essence, the BKE is more or less a small seated e-scooter, sometimes referred to as a “no-ped”.

Despite looking like the kind of concept vehicle that might have been whipped up for an auto show, Toyota states the BKE has actually been under development for several years.

A small team of chassis and electrical engineers has reportedly been testing and refining the design based on real-world use and feedback.

The basic idea came from a fairly simple question: How could Toyota make short-distance mobility easier and integrate it more seamlessly into everyday life?

The result is essentially a secondary vehicle designed to travel inside your primary vehicle.

Toyota specifically highlights camping, errands, last-mile transportation, and even using the BKE as a pit bike alongside a GR86. The bike can also be recharged from the 110V AC outlets found in many Toyota vehicles, meaning the car carrying it can effectively serve as its mobile charging station.

Sources indicate that believe it or not, Toyota Chairman Akio Toyoda has apparently been involved in the testing process himself. Toyoda attracted attention after riding a similar small electric mobility device around the 2025 Japan Mobility Show, and Toyota says his experience riding prototypes has even resulted in design changes.

After Toyoda complained about getting splashed while riding through puddles, for example, engineers enlarged the rear fender.

It’s a small detail, but it’s also a pretty textbook example of Toyota’s famous kaizen philosophy of continuous improvement.

Here’s where things get a little frustrating for those of us who want to know what the BKE can actually do.

Industry observers note that toyota hasn’t announced the motor power, battery capacity, range, top speed, or even the vehicle’s weight. There’s also no pricing because, for now, there’s nothing to buy.

Toyota is referring to the BKE strictly as a concept and hasn’t confirmed production plans or a timetable for bringing it to market.

But the fact that Toyota claims a small engineering team has spent several years developing and testing the BKE makes it more interesting than your typical one-off styling exercise.

And the underlying idea makes a lot of sense.

It has been revealed that I’m obviously a big believer in matching the vehicle to the trip. Taking a 4,000-pound car several miles to move one person isn’t always the most efficient solution, and a compact electric two-wheeler gives drivers an easy way to leave the larger vehicle behind for those shorter trips.

Toyota itself makes essentially the same argument, saying that using smaller vehicles for shorter journeys could reduce emissions by better matching the vehicle to the task.

There’s also something amusingly circular about one of the world’s largest automakers arriving at the conclusion that sometimes the best vehicle for a trip is a tiny electric bike.

Recent findings suggest that but hey, I’ll take it. Now Toyota just needs to actually build the thing – and preferably tell us how fast it goes first.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The FIA began the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend by announcing that all manufacturers have agreed to the framework to bring turbocharged V8 engines back to F1 and move away from the current V6 turbo.

This move has long been expected, with hopes that it will make engine building easier and cheaper while bringing back the sound that motorsport fans deeply miss.

The sound of the V8 engines was a rally cry for fans and has been sorely missed by audiences worldwide.

The F1 engine manufacturers agreed to a rough-out overarching proposal to move to a 2.1-liter turbocharged V8 from 2030 onwards, with a lower charge of electrical power reducing the hybrid output from 350kW to 200kW, a decrease of nearly 56 percent.

The FIA unveiled that ‘The plan is to marry the V8 power unit to a chassis which will also be lighter, more agile and placing greater emphasis on driver skill and close racing.”.

With everyone in agreement, PU manufacturers will start to jockey between improving the new car entering a sophomore season of new regulations and game planning for the major change coming just three seasons down the line.

It’s been 13 years since manufacturers last built a V8 engine for F1.

In a recent development, “This agreement marks a significant milestone in shaping the future of Formula 1,” FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem said. “From the outset, I have been clear in my ambition to deliver a sport that is more competitive and more exciting for our fans, while remaining at the forefront of innovation and sustainability.

“The return of V8 engines represents an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA of this Championship, bringing back the sound, emotion and pure racing that is loved worldwide. Our vision is clear, lighter, simpler and more affordable cars that put driver skill at the heart of the competition.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some mid-cycle updates focus on aesthetics, bringing some latest style (and hopefully some new eyes) to a slightly older product. The 2027 Toyota Sienna skipped those pleasantries and focused on the meat and potatoes: its hybrid powertrain.

Sources indicate that the 2027 Toyota Sienna looks no different—unless you count the Cypress paint color, which was dropped and swapped with Storm Cloud—but it’s what’s lying under the body that matters more here. The Sienna adopts Toyota’s sixth-generation hybrid powertrain, which first arrived in the upscale Lexus ES Hybrid. A new electric motor packs more efficient silicon-carbide conductors, and it pairs with a 1.15-kWh battery that ditches the old nickel-metal hydride chemistry in favor of lithium-ion. In addition, there’s a whole new electrical platform underpinning it all, with new ECUs and software to manage everything.

See all results for latest 2027 Toyota Sienna for sale near 60193.

Combine all that with a 2.5-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine that has been retuned for quieter low-speed operation, and you have a Toyota Sienna that produces a whopping six horsepower more than before, rising from 245 horses to 251. Engine torque is unchanged at 176 pound-feet, and Toyota did not specify e-motor torque. That small power bump is enough to affect its acceleration: Toyota estimates a 7.5-second sprint to 60 mph in front-wheel-drive Sienna variants, rising to 7.6 seconds with AWD. That’s 0.3 or 0.4 second quicker than before, respectively.

Even with that bump in speed, Toyota claims improved fuel economy in the 2027 Sienna, to the tune of +3 mpg in the city for FWD models and +4 mpg in the city for AWD models. Combined estimates rise 1 or 2 mpg. For context, the 2026 model is EPA estimated at 36 mpg city/36 highway/36 combined for the front-driver, and 35/36/35 for the AWD.

There have also been some tweaks to other electrical-adjacent components. The electronic power steering promises less effort at low speeds, while improving on-center feel at highway speeds. That adjustment includes a new steering-wheel layout that will eventually migrate to other sixth-gen-equipped hybrids. Toyota also fiddled with its brake electronics, resulting in less pedal effort and a smoother blend between regen and friction braking. The Sienna also includes something Toyota calls Vehicle Braking Posture Control, which applies braking to individual wheels with the aim to reduce body roll during cornering.

Creature comforts get some upgrades as well. A 12.3-inch infotainment screen is now standard across the lineup (the LE grade ditches its 8.0-incher), as is a 12.3-inch gauge cluster (LE and XLE get this instead of the old 7.0-inch getup). There’s latest LED cabin lighting, plus a revised rear-seat entertainment system that now features native apps on a new touchscreen. Upgraded dashboard sound abatement promises to lower the cabin volume by one decibel.

See all results for fresh 2027 Toyota Sienna for sale near 60193.

Industry observers note that toyota also slimmed down the Sienna’s trims for 2027. The Limited grade has been dropped in favor of adding more features to the sporty XSE variant, which rises to become the trim underneath the Platinum. As a result, the 2027 Sienna XSE picks up niceties like ventilated front seats with memory, a panoramic-view monitor, and a head-up display. The rugged Woodland Edition trim also picks up the surround-view tech. The upgraded rear-seat entertainment is available on the Woodland, XSE, and Platinum trims.

According to recent reports, the 2027 Toyota Sienna reaches dealerships in early—you guessed it—2027. Pricing starts around $44,500 for the front-wheel-drive LE base trim, which represents a price bump of less than $2000 over a base 2026 Sienna. Not too shabby for a whole fresh generation of powertrain.

Recent findings suggest that the Rivian R2 may be a little tamer than its bigger brothers, the R1S and R1T, but that doesn’t mean that the aftermarket world can’t chime in and lend a helping hand. While the mid-size SUV carried over many of its larger siblings’ characteristics, it lacks one feature that could make the difference between getting back home the same day and spending hours trying to get unstuck: adjustable air suspension.

The R2 comes with fixed suspension, so the driver has to be very careful when choosing their lines, but thankfully, there are now a handful of companies out there that sell suspension lift kits for the R2.

Sources indicate that bullray Manufacturing made a custom lift kit for a Rivian R2 that’s used as a chase truck for the Off Grid racing team. The electric SUV, an R2 Performance, made an appearance at this year’s SEMA show in Las Vegas and was filmed by Out of Spec Bits.

Recent findings suggest that the 2.0-inch metal lifters were fitted above the dampers, and the electric crossover retains its standard semi-active suspension. In other words, this is a body lift, not a suspension lift, but it shouldn’t matter too much, considering this is a unibody vehicle, after all. The high-voltage battery and electric motors are fitted directly to the underside of the body, so the added ground clearance should help protect vital components when going off the beaten track.

It’s also worth noting that EV Sportline, a firm that specializes in aftermarket parts for electric vehicles, offers a 1.6-inch body lift kit for the Rivian R2.

According to recent reports, getting back to the green R2 that went to SEMA, it’s obvious that it’s fully kitted out for any overlanding experience. There’s a Baja Designs 40-inch light bar, a set of Maxtrax Extreme recovery boards, plenty of storage options on the roof, and a Rig’D tire carrier at the rear. A set of Yokohama Geolandar Mud-Terrain tires wrapped around 17-inch Method Racing wheels completes the look.

Inside, there’s a communications system, as well as a racing-spec GPS navigation system for the front passenger.

Sources indicate that all in all, it looks really badass and reveals that there’s a lot of potential in the aftermarket space for the Rivian R2. Clearly, the raised ride height and chunky tires will eat into the car’s official 330-mile range, but that’s to be expected.

Latest Update: The best way to pack a suitcase, according to science

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1509 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • While recently packing for an overseas excursion, I stuffed every spare space I could find in my carry-on.
  • To find out how best to pack according to science, Popular Science turned to Anne McAlpin, a travel expert and author of the book, Pack it Up: the Essential Guide to Smart Travel.
  • Recent findings suggest that many carry-on bags have “ruts” or internal grooves to accommodate a recessed trolley handle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While recently packing for an overseas excursion, I stuffed every spare space I could find in my carry-on. I used what I call the “Mary Poppins” packing method: willing myself to believe that whatever I wanted to put in my luggage would fit, regardless of the size of the object or the size of my bag. Somehow my system worked, but when I arrived at my destination and unzipped my bag, everything within it exploded onto the floor. “There’s gotta be a better way,” I thought.

To find out how best to pack according to science, Popular Science turned to Anne McAlpin, a travel expert and author of the book, Pack it Up: the Essential Guide to Smart Travel. Over the course of her lifetime, McAlpin has estimated she’s packed—and unpacked—more than 25,000 times! She’s a whiz at minimizing dead space, maximizing volume, and keeping clothes looking more like they came off a closet hanger than straight out of a laundry bin.

Recent findings suggest that many carry-on bags have “ruts” or internal grooves to accommodate a recessed trolley handle. This handle uses two narrow metal poles that retract straight into the middle or sides of the interior lining, causing the interior surface of the suitcase to be uneven.

“If you don’t have a flat foundation, make one,” says McAlpin. Having a flat foundation maximizes space, prevents wrinkles, and adds stability to your bag. To do this, consider evening out the space between ruts with packing or compression cubes. “You can put all of your underwear into a compression cube,” a small bag made of breathable nylon or polyester mesh used in part to organize items, and then place it between the ruts. This will even out the bottom of a hard-shell suitcase. Flexible items such as toiletry kits and rolled-up socks can help to form this base layer as well. “I then pack my clothing on top of that flat foundation.”.

Recent findings suggest that mcAlpin puts her shoes (she usually packs two pairs and wears a third) towards the bottom of the suitcase so that the weight is on the wheels. “You don’t want to put your heavy items on the top of the inside of your suitcase,” she says. “This will cause it to constantly topple.”.

When it comes to clothing, McAlpin rolls some items and flat packs others. “I call it interlayering,” she notes.

Recent findings suggest that for example, with pants, rather than folding them to stack in a pile, McAlpin lays each pair out along its natural creases as if she were going to put them on a hanger. Then, she places them in her suitcase: waistband at the top of one side of the bag, legs dangling out the other side of the bag. They’re not folded, but laid out straight. This way, McAlpin can then wrap them around the rolled items that she’ll later place on top of them.

Industry observers note that she does the same with cotton shirts, sundresses—anything that might wrinkle. With each item, McAlpin alternates the direction, so that there are no two waistbands or shirt collars bulking up one side of the suitcase.

It has been revealed that “I then roll my knit items and synthetic things that don’t wrinkle as much. I roll them up like Tootsie Rolls and I place them side by side,” in the middle of the laid-out items. While folding clothes and stacking them leaves pockets of air both inside the folds and within the layers, rolling wraps fabrics into a smooth, tight cylinder, which reduces the overall amount of space each item uses. It’s the best of both worlds! Your laid-out items aren’t as wrinkled and your wrinkle-resistant items are more tightly packed. This allows for more room in your suitcase overall.

According to recent reports, when McAlpin has all her rolled items tightly packed together, she takes the pant legs and skirts that are still hanging off the sides of the suitcase, and “bends them up and over the ‘roll bar’ I’ve made of sweaters, pajamas, and sweats.” This helps avoid the knee creases that come when you’re simply folding pants. It also keeps items compact, and is a game-changer when it comes to unpacking. You can just lift all of the interlayered items out of your suitcase in one fell swoop.

Recent findings suggest that fill up empty space. For example, McAlpin states that if you’re a couple packing together, you may be able to slide a woman’s sandal right into a man’s shoe, or at least use the shoe’s interior cavity to store phone chargers, socks, or small items like earrings and even an eyeglasses case. Not only is it a space-saver, but filling up unused space prevents transit damage by keeping items inside from shifting.

Sources indicate that stuff the corners of a suitcase with socks, rolled-up t-shirts, etc, “because all those awkward corners offer prime packing space,” states McAlpin. Filling up those pockets also distributes structural stress throughout the bag, helping to keep features like zippers and fabric intact during excessive handling.

Industry observers note that why do we put seatbacks up for landing? An aviation expert explains.

Another trick: laying belts around the luggage perimeter so that they’re easier to find.

Industry observers note that to keep things condensed and organized, McAlpin suggests compression cubes. These small bags feature two zippers: a main zipper that closes the cube like a standard bag, and a second perimeter zipper that pulls the cube’s top and bottom panels closer together, squeezing out excess air and reducing volume. Compression cubes help eliminate air pockets that come with traditional folding and can reduce the volume of soft clothes like T-shirts and pants up to 30 percent.

Another option: roll-up compression bags. These pump-free, vacuum-free storage bags use one-way pressure valves to push air out, cutting volume by up to 80 percent. “I use these for laundry,” notes McAlpin, because they temporarily block odors.

It has been revealed that “They’re like an industrial Ziploc bag,” she says, and great for bulky items like a fleece jacket. But use them sparingly. Roll sacks are typically made of plastic and cause a lot more wrinkles than traditional compression cubes.

Sources indicate that mcAlpin carries dry laundry sheets and a two-gallon Ziploc bag for washing clothes. “The bag doesn’t take up any room, and then I can wash my socks and underwear without worrying if I’ve left any toothpaste in the sink.”.

McAlpin states her packing “3:1 ratio” (three tops to every bottom) has “changed people’s lives.” She packs nine tops and three bottoms, and everything mixes and matches. “I base everything around two colors,” she says, “like a black and a tan,” and then throws in an occasional splash of color.

This works, says McAlpin, because human memory registers outfits based on what’s closest to the head and face. And while she travels with three pairs of shoes, each one should be for something different. For example, runners for long walks, sandals for the beach, and loafers for evenings.

As for the bag itself, McAlpin claims four-wheel bags (spinner luggage) are a must. Not only are they easy to maneuver through packed terminals and airplane aisles, the ability to push the bag upright beside you keeps your arm in a neutral, bent-elbow position. This places less stress on your wrists, shoulders, and lower back compared to pulling a two-wheel bag behind you, and plays a big role in easing ergonomic strain.

In a recent development, they’re also ideal for stacking, since they stay upright. Think about it, says McAlpin. “When you pack your heavy tote bag on top of your suitcase, it’s the bag, not your shoulders, that’s carrying the weight.”.

Ultimately, the idea is to make use of all your space, keep items from bumping around inside your suitcase and (if possible) wrinkle-free, and to not throw out your back in the process.

Sources indicate that of course, when it comes to finding room for souvenirs, there’s always the Mary Poppins packing method. But after talking with McAlpin, I’ve been using her method exclusively. My clothes, formerly creased, rumpled, and crinkled, are now decidedly wrinkle-free!
