📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that peel the name tags off the Mazda Cosmo, and it could easily pass for an American car.
  • The Cosmo is something of a mystery car.
  • In Japan, the Cosmo is last season’s smash hit, named Car of the Year by one of the country’s auto mag­azines and the next best thing in Tokyo to driving a foreign car.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From the April 1977 issue of Car and Driver.

It has been revealed that peel the name tags off the Mazda Cosmo, and it could easily pass for an American car. The two-rotor Wankel is as smooth and vibra­tionless as any V-8, the car is easily as quiet inside as a typical intermediate sedan, and the Cosmo’s body even has the same sort of creaky flexibility that we’ve come to expect of Detroit cars. If we didn’t know better, we might think this was a upcoming subcompact Buick or perhaps a miniature Camaro. Never would we confuse it with a Toyota or Datsun.

The Cosmo is something of a mystery car. It was designed with the United States in mind—a fast, smooth sports coupe for a country that swallowed Datsun Z-cars as fast as the ships could unload them at the ports. But for some reason, the Cosmo never struck the American fancy. Maybe it was the bad publicity heaped on the rotary engine; per­haps the dull colors and unfortunate combi­nation of mag wheels and white-wall tires turned off the sporty-car buyer. And we can’t entirely disregard the thought that a coupe with a Vega silhouette, Oldsmobile waterfall grille, and Plymouth Cricket taillights may sim­ply be the wrong thing to wave in American faces. But whatever the reason, Cosmos tend to languish in the showrooms.

See all results for used cars for sale near 07011.

That’s the situation in the U.S. In Japan, the Cosmo is last season’s smash hit, named Car of the Year by one of the country’s auto mag­azines and the next best thing in Tokyo to driving a foreign car. (The Japanese, like many Americans, tend to think that anything imported is probably better and certainly more fun than the made-at-home equivalent). The car looks great in its own neighborhood. It has slightly different—but not much small­er—bumpers and the mandatory mirrors perched out on the front fenders halfway to the headlights. But apart from those two de­tails, the Japanese-market Cosmo looks the same as the one we tend to ignore here.

According to recent reports, we humbly submit, at this point, that the Cosmo deserves another look, if for no other reason than it features one commodity in de­cidedly short supply elsewhere—horsepower. This car is quick. The engine is wide awake above 2000 rpm, and it climbs to 7000 with­out a backward glance. Freeways abound with legions of 350 four-barrels that won’t match the Cosmo’s pace. And as amazing as it may seem, none of them can come close to the Mazda’s gas mileage. The 1977 model with the standard five-speed trans­mission has been weaned down to 32 mpg highway and 20 mpg city for a combined rating of 25 mpg in the EPA mileage sweep­stakes. That is excellent economy for a car of this performance level.

While the Cosmo is surprisingly economical, it is by no means austere. The interior offers about the same amount of useful space for four occupants as a Camaro, and the trunk, because it stows its spare more ef­ficiently than the Chevrolet, is at least as good. Yet overall, the Mazda Cosmo is about the same size as a Corvette, actually slightly smaller.

See all results for used cars for sale near 07011.

The quality of the interior is also on par with that of Detroit models. The dash is molded vinyl with a minimum of seams, and shows the driver a full complement of instruments set in a field of imitation wood. Velour cloth covers the seats and door panels. There is even a trapezoid opera window to delight the double-knit crowd. And if that doesn’t knock them dead at the Donut Center, show them the wire-spoked steering wheel.

According to recent reports, there is just one aspect of the Mazda’s er­satz Detroit personality with which we take is­sue: It’s a smooth-road car. On ribbons of un­broken concrete the Cosmo simply glides along, but when the going gets rough, so does the ride. The front wheels steer notice­ably over bumps, and the suspension travel is limited enough so that the wheels are occa­sionally jerked clear of the road on surfaces that are not really that rough. The balance of the car, particularly on smooth roads, is rea­sonable however.

It has been revealed that at least the Cosmo’s ailments are the kind that can be fixed, certainly by a second look at the factory and perhaps even with a few bolt-on aftermarket parts. We would start with the shocks and see what happens. The rotary engine, on the other hand, is just fine as it is. And Mazda provides an incredible warranty—­five years or 75,000 miles—to make sure it stays that way. Nobody can dislike a car that is guaranteed to keep running even after the loan is paid off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now launched, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

Sources indicate that the recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was announced last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy launched, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

The trial goes live today at 4am PT, 7am ET, 12pm GMT across all platforms, and will be available for a week; ending Tuesday, December 2. It includes three core maps: Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields.

Players will have access to four game modes, played on different versions of the same maps. Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch will all be available to choose from, and there don’t appear to be any level or XP limits in the trial.

Unfortunatley, just as the free trial was about to go live, the game got hit with a major matchmaking outage that took down all matchmaking in the core game, leaving Redsec unaffected.

Hopefully EA can resolve this issue before the trial officially kicks off.

Industry News: Spyker's CEO Wants You to ‘Drive the Hell’ Out of His $1.8 Million Supercars

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (721 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When people spend nearly $2 million on a two-seat, mid-engine car, you can safely assume it is not the only car in their garage.
  • Industry observers note that but Spyker CEO Victor Muller has a different idea.
  • Industry observers note that that's a refreshing philosophy from someone selling a car this pricey.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When people spend nearly $2 million on a two-seat, mid-engine car, you can safely assume it is not the only car in their garage. It makes sense that it will not be driven every day; however, often times cars like this are not really driven at all. They spend their entire lives in climate-controlled garages, tucked beneath soft covers. And when the car in question is something like a one-of-25 C8 Preliator XXV Coupé, the temptation to preserve it as a collectible is understandable.

Industry observers note that but Spyker CEO Victor Muller has a different idea. He wants his customers to get behind the wheel and drive. "We prefer to sell our cars to people that actually use them," Muller told me during an interview at Retromobile New York. "Because that's what I made them for. To drive the hell out of them.".

Industry observers note that that's a refreshing philosophy from someone selling a car this pricey. Particularly when that car is the latest C8 Preliator XXV Coupé, which looks as much like a piece of fine jewelry as an 800-horsepower road rocket. Unfortunately, Muller admits that many of Spyker's previous creations haven't enjoyed particularly active lives.

Industry observers note that "Many of our cars, of the 252 we made so far, have just ended up in dungeons, in vaults, in spaces where nobody will ever see them," Muller noted. He's hoping to change that by organizing more owner events and encouraging customers to spend time enjoying their cars; Spyker has joined the Supercar Owners Circle, a global network of car collectors, and is planning gatherings in Europe and the United States.

The firm is also in a position where it can be selective about who gets its cars. According to Muller, all 25 Preliator XXV Coupés sold during their debut at The Quail, a Motorsports Gathering in August. Every single one was snapped up in a day. "I've never seen anything like that in my entire life," he said. Spyker prepares to build 25 Spyders and 25 Sedancas in 2028, he added, once production of the Coupés is complete next year.

Sources indicate that who is buying these cars has changed dramatically over the last quarter century. "In 2000, my typical customer was a fifty-five to sixty-year-old industrialist—old money, car collector, very astute buyer," Muller explained. "Fast forward twenty five years. Your average age is thirty-five years. Tech investor. Huge collection. Knows his cars completely. But nobody asks how much it is.".

Sources indicate that muller notes approximately 40 percent of his latest buyers are existing or former Spyker owners, and roughly 80 percent of the new cars are expected to go to the United States. But no matter how old the buyer is or where they live, Muller wants them to drive the cars. This makes sense when you understand his approach to engineering; The new car has no massive infotainment screens or hybrid systems, and electronic intervention is largely limited to essential safety features like ABS and stability control.

“If you mis-shift in a Spyker and you drive two hundred miles an hour and you shift to second gear, you blow up the engine," Muller said. "And I think it has to be that way in Spyker world." For Spyker, the connection between driver and machine is more notable than chasing lap records, acceleration figures and electronic nannies. "If you don't like that, buy something else," he added. "If not, man up—drive a Spyker.".

Another way to demonstrate that these cars are meant to be driven is to get the brand back into racing. Muller revealed that Spyker is taking steps toward returning to professional endurance competition. The company competed in the 24 Hours of Le Mans eight times, most recently in 2010. Naturally, I asked whether another trip to Le Mans might be in Spyker's future.

"Absolutely," Muller said. "We'd love to go back in racing." Muller indicates Spyker is preparing to re-enter endurance racing, although he stopped short of announcing a timeline, championship, or confirmed race entry. He certainly likes the idea of seeing his latest creation on the track. More importantly, he's already started putting people in place to make it happen.

"I actually hired my former GT2 race director again," Muller mentioned. "He started a week ago today.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China’s SC01 electric sports car, which wowed reviewers for its great handling and back-to-basics approach to EVs, is getting its own European factory, with a scheduled production start in May 2027.

The two-door EV, which was developed by Tianjin Gongjiangpai Auto Technology (TGAT), will be assembled at a new facility in central Italy by FIPA Europe, a company that currently makes Chinese microcars. The importer has signed a contract for an existing industrial complex in the Marche region, and work is expected to begin early next year, according to Electrive.

It has been revealed that the first phase of the European SC01 program involves a 20,000-square-meter (21,527-square-feet) production space and 50 employees who will work to assemble the electric two-seater from kits shipped from China. A 2,750-square-meter (29,600 sq ft) warehouse and a 20,000-square-meter (21,5278 sq ft) logistics area are also planned for the new facility.

It has been revealed that however, that’s just the start, as FIPA Europe intends to expand the floor space and its headcount by the end of the decade, with 285 jobs expected by the last day of 2030. The organization, which assembles the Desner T80, a low-speed electric microcar, claims to be the only authorized importer and manufacturer of the SC01 for the European Union and the only company responsible for the car’s European homologation.

The first SC01 prototypes are reportedly already roaming Italy’s streets, imported from China for development purposes. The next step is to install the assembly lines at the fresh factory in the first quarter of 2027, with the first Italian-built SC01s scheduled to roll out the door in May.

Recent findings suggest that as a reminder, the Chinese-spec SC01 is powered by a 430-horsepower (320-kilowatt) dual-motor powertrain that draws electricity from a 60-kilowatt-hour battery pack. The car was developed with backing from tech giant Xiaomi and is assembled in China by JMEV, a joint venture between Groupe Renault and Jiangling Motors Corporation Group.

Recent findings suggest that the car’s biggest trait is its low weight. Tipping the scales at less than 1,400 kilograms (3,086 pounds), it’s lighter than a Porsche 911 and can sprint from zero to 62 mph (0-100 kilometers per hour) in 2.9 seconds. What’s more, the car’s dual-motor powertrain can be configured to work either independently or together, so the driver can choose from rear-wheel drive, front-wheel drive, or all-wheel drive.

Inside, there’s just the bare minimum, with a digital instrument cluster and a few physical controls on the center console. There’s no infotainment screen, let alone a passenger display, as is the case with many modern luxury cars nowadays.

Pricing hasn’t been announced for the European version of the SC01, but in China, the back-to-basics EV retails for the equivalent of about $32,000.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota is overhauling its best-selling vehicle of all time, which will include the first fully electric Corolla.

The Toyota Corolla is one of the most recognized and best-selling automotive nameplates of all time.

Since its debut in 1966, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla thanks to its reliability, low cost of ownership, efficiency, and affordable price tag.

Toyota sells the Corolla in more than 150 countries and has expanded the lineup over the past 50 years from sedans and hatchbacks to coupes, wagons, a sporty GR Corolla, and the Corolla Cross compact SUV.

For its 13th generation, Toyota is planning a major overhaul that’s expected to be its biggest transformation yet.

The next-gen Toyota Corolla will be based on a fresh “multipathway” platform that will support gas, hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and, for the first time, fully electric powertrains.

“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle ― whatever the power source ― let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive!” Toyota’s former president and current CEO Koji Sato said after unveiling the Corolla Concept at the Japan Mobility Show last October.

In a recent development, toyota has kept most details a secret, including battery and powertrain specs. However, the fresh version is expected to adopt a similar design to the concept.

“When we created the concept, we wanted to give the Corolla name a new twist,” Norihiko Kobayashi, who has led the Corolla program since 2011, told Motor.es during a recent interview.

The Corolla has undergone several minor updates over the past 60 years, but the next-gen model will look nothing like its predecessors.

“It wasn’t simply about following in the footsteps of the past,” Kobayashi explained, “we wanted to delve into the future while still maintaining the Corolla identity.”.

Developing the next-gen Corolla “wasn’t just about making a newly introduced car, but about redefining the future without looking back,” he added.

Like the current version, the new Toyota Corolla will come in several different body types, including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and a GR variant.

The Corolla was the entry level vehicle for a lot of people before they could afford the Camry or the Lexus.

Details have yet to be confirmed, but the Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations and offer a pure electric driving range of at least 250 miles.

According to recent reports, the hybrid will reportedly use a upcoming 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the hybrid system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.

Sources indicate that toyota’s next-gen Corolla is expected to debut sometime in 2027 as a 2028 model year. According to Car and Driver, the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.

Earlier this month, the next-gen Toyota Corolla Cross was spotted testing for the first time (see the images here).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if the Fast & Furious franchise taught us anything, it’s that there’s always another gear, and there’s no such thing as a bad plot­line. (Also: family.) To honor its silver anniversary, here’s a recap of the F&F universe, as it expanded from the L.A. street-racing scene to encompass every action-film trope, device, and format ever scrawled on a Hollywood studio whiteboard.

The Fast and the Furious (2001).

Cop Brian O’Connor infiltrates the L.A. import-car scene to bust hijackers who steal DVD players and at least one sweet 13-inch TV/VCR combo. He bonds with bald kingpin Dominic Toretto, then lets him go. Executives smell a sequel. Toretto has other aims: The Chronicles of Riddick. Danger to manifold: 10/10.

Now a fugitive with a Nissan Skyline but no visible means of support, Brian joins the feds to catch a drug lord who tortures a corrupt cop with the ol’ rat-in-the-ice-bucket trick. Roman Pearce replaces Dom as the bald guy at the emotional core. Camaro jumps onto yacht. Danger to manifold: 5/10.

The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift (2006).

The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift (2006).

According to recent reports, brian who? Now it’s Sean, a high schooler who looks like he’s 35. Busted for street racing, he’s sent to Tokyo, the capital of street racing. He crosses the yakuza-­connected Drift King and falls in with Han Seoul-­Oh, who can’t stop snacking. Dom cameo as sequel bait. Danger to manifold: 七/10.

Dom’s back, and the crew now executes road-train robberies in the Dominican Republic. Brian, now FBI, infiltrates a heroin pipeline. Letty dies. Dom seeks vengeance. A Road Warrior–style chase ends in a killer wheelie, literally. Dom is busted, but a sequel is nigh. Danger to manifold: 3/10.

Street racing? Nah. We’re a heist franchise, dog. Dom’s crew, now fully Hollywood four-quadrant tested, steals a crime lord’s fortune in Brazil. A former wrestler shows up as DSS agent Luke Hobbs. Bald jokes and legal ambiguity ensue. Everybody walks with $100 million. Danger to manifold: 1.5/10.

Recent findings suggest that hobbs is back, and we meet British scoundrel number one, Owen Shaw, an ex-SAS mercenary who drives a ramp car that flips police cruisers like a spatula. Letty is alive (huh?), with amnesia, and on Shaw’s payroll. Gisele dies. (Who’s Gisele again?) Danger to manifold: –10/10.

Jason Statham (really?) is Deckard Shaw, Owen’s scoundrel brother, who fireballs Dom’s family home. The crew parachutes into Azerbaijan in their cars. A Lykan HyperSport jumps between three Abu Dhabi office towers. Han’s dead (like we believe that). The saddest ending imaginable. Danger to manifold: N/A.

Fate, F9, Fast X, Hobbs & Shaw (2017–23).

Roll call: John Cena. Dame Helen Mirren. Charlize Theron. Jason Momoa. Sir Idris Elba. Old villains are in the crew now. We’re in Cuba (thanks, Obama), Antarctica, a sub­marine, and a Pontiac Fiero in space. Han? Gisele? Both alive. It’s just a parody of action movies now, right? Danger to manifold: $7 billion/10.

A fresh Arc Raiders patch has arrived, bringing a host of latest fixes to several exploits players have recently been relying on to do things they’re not supposed to, and bypass certain mechanics to get into areas without having to go through proper channels.

The patch is fairly small, and surprisingly doesn’t include any buffs or nerfs to anything in particular.

Recent findings suggest that the list of notes for patch 1.4.0 is compact, with a clear focus on addressing several exploits. The biggest one, of course, is the addition of “exploit mitigation mechanisms” to stop players from glitching through locked doors.

Sources indicate that this fix applies to all maps, and it’s intended to address an issue whereby players would not bring the required keys to access those areas of the various maps. Locked rooms, if they can be unlocked, often hide a wealth of high-tier and rare loot.

But players have also been using similar exploits to clip through walls and access areas outside the playspace, allowing them to ambush enemy players and set up traps that would be impossible for others to detect.

It has been revealed that the game’s recent patch, which was released exactly one week ago, mainly consisted of balance tweaks to some of the more popular weapons and mines. However, it also introduced a few fixes to prevent players from clipping through walls by using barricades.

While on the subject of being in places where you’re not supposed to, the patch blocked exterior access to the locked room inside Spaceport's Control Tower, making it only accessible from inside the tower.

1.4.0 also fixes an especially nasty exploit that allowed players to bring up their weapons much faster than normal by promptly swapping to the quick use menu. There’s a range of smaller fixes for lighting and texture bugs here, too, and you can read all about it in the full change log below:.

#155297. Why obesity affects men and women differently may be hiding in their fat

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1096 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Why obesity affects men and women differently may be hiding in their fat

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1096 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that scientists at the University of California, Riverside have uncovered a surprising difference in how the immune systems of males and females respond to obesity.
  • The discovery centers on eosinophils, immune cells best known for their involvement in allergies and asthma.
  • The study, published in PNAS Nexus, was led by University of California, Riverside biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that scientists at the University of California, Riverside have uncovered a surprising difference in how the immune systems of males and females respond to obesity. Their findings suggest that certain immune cells found in body fat can help protect against inflammation and metabolic problems, while others may make these harmful effects worse.

The discovery centers on eosinophils, immune cells best known for their involvement in allergies and asthma. In experiments with mice, researchers found that these cells behave differently depending on biological sex, potentially helping explain why obesity does not affect males and females in the same way.

The study, published in PNAS Nexus, was led by University of California, Riverside biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik. Their findings challenge the longstanding assumption that eosinophils are largely similar cells with relatively few specialized functions. The results also point toward potential fresh approaches for treating obesity and its complications.

Six Types of Immune Cells Found in Body Fat.

Sources indicate that to investigate the role of eosinophils in obesity, the researchers used high-resolution single-cell sequencing, a technique that allows scientists to examine gene activity in individual cells. They identified six distinct eosinophil populations in adipose (fat) tissue, each with its own pattern of gene expression and potentially different biological functions.

This unexpected diversity suggests that eosinophils play a much more complicated role in metabolic health than previously recognized.

"Eosinophils are more complex than we once thought," said Nair, a professor of biomedical sciences in the UCR School of Medicine. "Some populations can protect against obesity, and if we can identify and activate the pathways that produce these protective cells, we may find new ways to improve metabolic health.".

Why Male and Female Fat Tissue Respond Differently.

One of the most striking discoveries was a difference in the immune cells found in male and female mice.

According to recent reports, female mice possessed a protective population of eosinophils that appeared to communicate more effectively with macrophages, another group of immune cells present in fat tissue. According to Nair, this cooperation may help create a healthier environment within fat tissue and support better metabolic function.

Male mice showed a different pattern. When given a diet high in fat, they were more likely to develop eosinophil populations associated with inflammation. Their fat tissue also contained eosinophils with gene activity patterns suggesting weaker protective functions.

These findings indicate that the effects of eosinophils on obesity depend on more than simply how many of these cells are present. The particular type of eosinophil and its interactions with neighboring immune cells may be equally notable.

"This means the relationship between eosinophils and obesity is not simply a matter of how many eosinophils are present," said Rebecca E. Ruggiero-Ruff, a postdoctoral researcher in Nair's lab and co-first author of the paper. "Their functional characteristics and how they communicate with other immune cells are also critical.".

A Protein That May Help Protect Against Inflammation.

The researchers also identified a protein called RELM alpha that appears to play an important role in maintaining the beneficial relationship between eosinophils and macrophages.

Sources indicate that produced by macrophages, RELM alpha seemed to help stabilize communication between the two immune cell types in female mice. This interaction may be one reason certain eosinophil populations are better able to support healthy fat tissue.

The finding builds on earlier experiments by the same research group, which showed that administering RELM alpha to mice produced protective effects. Together, the results suggest that the protein may help regulate immune activity within fat tissue and influence how the body responds to obesity.

Could the Discovery Lead to Better Obesity Treatments?

It has been revealed that although the results offer latest insight into the biology of obesity, the experiments were conducted in mice. Researchers have also detected eosinophils in fat tissue from people with obesity, but scientists do not yet fully understand what these cells do in the human body.

Recent findings suggest that nair cautioned that additional research will be necessary before the discovery can be used to develop treatments. One particularly important question is whether therapies targeting the immune system would work differently in men and women.

"A drug may not activate the same pathways or produce the same effects in males and females, particularly when it targets the immune system," said co-first author Xinru Qiu, a postdoctoral researcher in Godzik's lab. "We need to investigate sex-specific biology more thoroughly so that treatments can be optimized for different patients.".

Understanding these differences could eventually help researchers design more personalized treatments for obesity and the metabolic complications associated with it.

Scientists Initiative to Recreate Human Fat Tissue in the Lab.

The research team is now investigating whether the protective behavior observed in mouse eosinophils can also be studied in human laboratory models.

Industry observers note that to accomplish this, the scientists are developing three-dimensional adipose organoids. These miniature laboratory models reproduce certain features of real fat tissue, allowing researchers to examine how eosinophils interact with fat cells and other components of their environment.

The goal is to determine whether changing communication between immune cells could encourage healthier responses in human fat tissue.

Sources indicate that "We ultimately hope to develop human adipose organoids that will allow us to investigate whether manipulating immune-cell communication can promote healthier tissue responses," said Godzik, a professor of biomedical sciences and the Bruce D. and Nancy B. Varner Presidential Endowed Chair in Cancer Research.

In a recent development, the findings raise the possibility that targeting specific immune cell populations, rather than treating all eosinophils as functionally identical, could eventually provide latest ways to address obesity and its complications. Whether the same protective mechanisms operate in humans remains an vital question for future research.

The research team also included Lauren Vance, Yuxin He, and Djurdjica Coss, who worked alongside Nair, Godzik, Ruggiero-Ruff, and Qiu.

Funding for the study came from the National Institutes of Health, the UCR School of Medicine, and the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine.

The research paper is titled "Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity.".

BYD Ti7 banned from the EU for copying the Land Rover Defender’s design

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1065 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A Dutch court has barred BYD from selling or building its Ti7 SUV anywhere in the European Union after ruling that it infringes Jaguar Land Rover’s registered design for the Land Rover Defender.
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s a sharp turnaround from 10 days ago, when the same court in The Hague handed BYD an early win in the Defender copycat fight.
  • The preliminary relief judge at the District Court of The Hague issued the ruling on Friday, November 20, in summary proceedings JLR brought against 11 BYD companies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A Dutch court has barred BYD from selling or building its Ti7 SUV anywhere in the European Union after ruling that it infringes Jaguar Land Rover’s registered design for the Land Rover Defender. Breaking the injunction costs BYD €100,000 per day, up to €10 million.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a sharp turnaround from 10 days ago, when the same court in The Hague handed BYD an early win in the Defender copycat fight. BYD’s Hong Kong shares fell as much as 4% on Monday before closing 1.9% lower.

The preliminary relief judge at the District Court of The Hague issued the ruling on Friday, November 20, in summary proceedings JLR brought against 11 BYD companies.

It has been revealed that JLR put six registered EU designs in front of the court. The judge only needed one of them: design 005248580-0004, registered in April 2018 and covering the current Defender 110, known internally as the L663.

According to recent reports, according to the ruling, the elements that dominate that design are the rounded “shoulders,” the rounded corners, the signature panel on the C-pillar, the rounded wheel-arch cutouts, the continuous window line, and the overall silhouette. The court found every one of them on the Ti7.

Here’s how the two SUVs compare from the same angles, using official press images from BYD and JLR:.

BYD argued that the headlights, grille, bumpers, hood and side profile are all different. Not enough, mentioned the judge, who ruled that those differences, on their own or combined, don’t give an informed user a different overall impression. The court also found the Ti7 sits closer to the Defender than to older boxy SUVs like the Ford Flex, Jeep Wrangler and Mercedes G-Class.

In a recent development, BYD doesn’t sell the Ti7 in the EU. It told the court it has “no concrete looks” to launch it there and that the SUV can only be ordered in the UK.

Sources indicate that the judge didn’t buy that as a defense. By BYD’s own account, it developed the seven-seat layout for the UK and Europe, a promotional video called the Ti7 the first seven-seat SUV “in Europe,” and BYD wouldn’t commit to keeping it out of the EU. That was enough for the court to find a threat of infringement.

So BYD’s EU entities can no longer import, produce, offer, sell, store or supply the Ti7. The order kicks in one week after the ruling is formally served, and it even covers BYD’s Hungarian unit, since the judge considered it conceivable the Ti7 could come out of the new Szeged factory.

In a recent development, the UK is a different story. The court said it has no jurisdiction over BYD UK and threw out JLR’s UK design claims, so British deliveries are still on for January 2027. That’s the one European market where BYD actually opened orders, pricing the Ti7 at £47,995, about £24,000 below the £71,840 plug-in Defender 110.

BYD stated it “strongly disagrees” with the judgment and will appeal, adding that the Ti7 “is the result of BYD’s own independent design work and infringes none of JLR’s rights.” JLR told AFP it protects its intellectual property and takes legal action when necessary.

BYD has four weeks to appeal, but the injunction stays in force while it does. JLR, for its part, has six months to file a full case on the merits, or BYD can get the injunction lifted.

This whole thing started in August, when JLR had bailiffs raid BYD’s Dutch offices in Schiedam and Hoofddorp. The court later ordered JLR to destroy everything it seized, saying it didn’t need BYD’s internal files to make its design case. And it didn’t. JLR won on the design registration alone.

The Ti7 looks like a Defender. We mentioned so when BYD first brought it to the UK, and so did pretty much everyone else. Chinese automakers have been building Defender lookalikes for years, but most of them stayed in China.

BYD brought one to the Defender’s home turf at a £24,000 discount, so a fight with JLR was always coming.

It has been revealed that as a consumer, I would consider one element extremely different between the two vehicles -- build quality. Land Rover has a reputation in that department. So does BYD. I would buy the BYD on that alone in the BBB (big,boxy,brick) "category" of vehicle. Is that what JLR is really worried about?

But honestly, all these boxy SUVs look the same to me.

It has been revealed that nobody owns “boxy.” JLR even failed to trademark the classic Defender’s shape in the UK, a fight it lost in its legal battle with the Ineos Grenadier. But it registered the newly introduced Defender’s design in 2018, and that specific combination of shoulders, C-pillar panel and wheel arches is exactly what the court protected. That’s how design rights are supposed to work.

Recent findings suggest that the actual business damage is small for now. The Ti7 sells roughly 30,000 units a month, almost all in China, and the UK launch goes ahead. The stock dip was about headlines more than lost Ti7 sales.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Physical buttons have a lot going for them. They’re easy to find by feel, satisfying to use, and generally pretty good at staying wherever the automaker installed them. Well, it seems Audi has an idea that would change that last part: it involves hiding the buttons behind a touchscreen, then deploying them when needed.

As CarMoses first discovered, Audi has filed for a patent application that describes a motorized switch bar, which pivots out from behind the display’s lower edge. The screen stays fixed, while the physical controls swing into position beneath it. Interestingly, when stowed, the bar apparently has an on-screen counterpart with the same functions lined up in the same order, so those who don't want physical buttons can avoid them entirely.

For those who do want the physical buttons, there are plenty of reasons to get excited. First, Audi states in its patent documents with the German government that the switches can deploy at startup, via voice controls, or via gestures. Moving the controls from the screen to the physical switches also provides more total screen room for consumers. (In one example, the physical bar deploys when a movie opens, leaving more room for the video.).

Ultimately, this could be a great way to meet the demands of more people. Designers love a clean dashboard without physical buttons and switches. Plenty of drivers really love having that switchgear. This system allows owners to pick whatever they want on the fly.

Recent findings suggest that the timing makes plenty of sense too. Audi has openly mentioned that it views moving toward more mechanical controls as the right direction. Of course, adding extra complexity to the once-simple idea of buttons also can increase the cost down the line when it comes time for repairs, but even so, this idea is certainly a fascinating solution to a very modern problem.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it’s no secret that electric cars are more affordable to maintain than their gasoline-powered counterparts. While they may have a higher purchase price than a comparable gas-powered vehicle, EVs can save owners money over time by eliminating the need for regular engine oil changes, emissions tests, and other traditional maintenance tasks. Affordable electric vehicles are also becoming increasingly common, with even more options expected to arrive in the coming years.

Recent findings suggest that however, that doesn't mean electric cars are completely maintenance-free. Like any other vehicle, EVs require regular care and attention to remain reliable and perform at their best for many years.

According to recent reports, although they don't have conventional combustion engines or traditional automatic transmissions, electric cars still feature components that require periodic maintenance. These include reduction gearboxes, brake fluid, brake pads, coolant systems, and tires among other things. Keeping these components in good condition is essential to ensuring an EV's long-term reliability.

ERANGE EV tires are purpose-built for electric vehicles, combining efficiency, comfort and performance with advanced EcoPoint3 technology.

Recent findings suggest that for the second installment of our EV maintenance series, I'll be taking a closer look at the Hyundai Ioniq 5, one of the most recognizable electric crossovers on the market. Made in the United States and South Korea, the Ioniq 5 has long been one of the biggest rivals to the ubiquitous Tesla Model Y.

I'll break down Hyundai's recommended maintenance schedule, explaining which items are required to keep the vehicle running smoothly over the long term.

It has been revealed that compared to Tesla, which is known for its rather skimpy maintenance blueprint, Hyundai includes a generous list of maintenance items in the owner’s manual. The automaker also includes additional service actions that should be performed if the car is used in harsher-than-normal conditions, so owners know what to expect in the long run.

In a recent development, there’s a normal maintenance schedule and a separate section for severe usage and low mileage conditions. Hyundai also has a list of maintenance items that can be performed by the owner. I’ll go through all of them, so drivers can easily mark down what needs to be done during the car’s lifetime.

Hyundai states that normal driving conditions include distances longer than 10 miles, clean roads without salt or dust, ambient temperatures under 90ºF (32ºC), no towing, no roof rack, and normal speeds. Under these conditions, the required maintenance for a Hyundai Ioniq 5 is as follows, according to the owner’s manual:.

According to Hyundai, extra precaution needs to be taken if the car is driven under certain conditions. These include repeated driving short distances of less than five miles in normal temperatures or less than 10 miles in freezing temperatures, and driving on rough, dusty, muddy, unpaved, graveled, or salt-spread roads.

But that’s not all. Driving in areas using salt or other corrosive materials, or in very cold weather, driving in heavy dust conditions, driving in heavy traffic areas with the ambient temperature higher than 90ºF (32 ºC) while consuming more than 50% of electric energy, and driving on uphill, downhill, or mountain roads repeatedly can also result in extra maintenance items.

Towing a trailer, using a roof rack, driving as a patrol car or taxi, frequently driving at high speeds, and frequently driving in stop-and-go conditions are also part of the conditions that lead to more intense servicing requirements.

In addition to the normal maintenance schedule above, Hyundai recommends the following actions for severe usage and low-mileage conditions:.

All of these items should be performed by a Hyundai technician, but the Ioniq 5 also has a consistent list of maintenance actions that should be performed by the owner.

The Hyundai Ioniq 5 is one of the best-selling electric crossovers in the United States, and for good reason. Its unique styling has plenty of fans, and it’s a genuinely nice car to drive. As for its maintenance requirements, the official recommendations have a lot more items compared to the Tesla Model Y, but at the end of the day, most of them are just inspection jobs. As a result, maintenance costs should be quite low compared to a comparable gas vehicle. Just rotate and replace tires, keep an eye on your brakes, and swap out the coolant after 10 years or 120,000 miles.

Tesla's EVs Could Get One Big Upgrade Next Year

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (510 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon loves to mash his companies together.
  • This came in response to X user David Marcus, who mentioned: "Can't wait for Tesla to offer an embedded Starlink option on all models (beyond the Cybercab).".
  • "Hopefully available toward the end of next year," he said in the X reply.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon loves to mash his companies together. He claims the Roadster has boosters from SpaceX, and the Cybercab has Starlink internet. And its coming to more Teslas, Musk said Monday. He claimed it will be available on all Tesla models by the end of 2027, though I don't put too much stake in his timelines generally.

This came in response to X user David Marcus, who mentioned: "Can't wait for Tesla to offer an embedded Starlink option on all models (beyond the Cybercab).".

Tesla CEO Elon Musk responded directly.

"Hopefully available toward the end of next year," he said in the X reply. "This will be important for unsupervised FSD, so passengers have high bandwidth everywhere for work and entertainment.".

Recent findings suggest that he did add a single caveat, though. "Except in China, as Starlink is illegal there.".

According to recent reports, all of the Cybercabs that recently launched in Dallas have Starlink antennas, Sawyer Merritt on X claims. It will be interesting to see how Tesla physically integrates Starlink into the back of other Tesla models, though. The Cybercab has its antennae panel built into the roof, and you can see its little square cutout. However, that would require redesigning the roof panels of all existing Tesla models, which isn't exactly easy. Unless owners would be cool with an additional panel being mounted on top of the car, like the major flat antennae we saw being tested on the Cybertruck recently.

However, according to Tesla's AI lead Ashok Elluswamy, Cybercab passengers presently can't connect to Starlink, as it's only used for fleet management, navigation, and customer service. So adding FSD assistance and passenger entertainment would be a couple of steps up from the robotaxi's capabilities.

Industry observers note that teslas with FSD are already pretty capable even where internet connection might be shoddy, such as on secluded trails. So it's unclear if Starlink will truly be all that necessary, but perhaps it will help with connection reliability in really remote areas. Especially now that FSD can show you a real time camera feed of your car's surroundings, so it looks like you're playing Grand Theft Auto with you own car in real life.

Elon's timelines are about as reliable as mine when I tell my wife I'm gonna mow the lawn on Football Sunday. However, the technology already seems like it's there with the Cybercab, and the patent is already filed. It's just a matter of integrating it into existing models.

Industry News: The best soft launch mobile games for iPhone, iPad or Android

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2445 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pocketgamer

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The biggest games yet to launch on the global market.
  • If you've been looking for something upcoming and exciting that isn't quite fully released, then look no further; you've found our list of the best games at the moment in soft launch.
  • Sometimes developers like to make sure the paying public is willing to play their game before they push it to every device in the world - that's where soft launch comes in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest games yet to launch on the global market.

If you've been looking for something upcoming and exciting that isn't quite fully released, then look no further; you've found our list of the best games at the moment in soft launch.

Sometimes developers like to make sure the paying public is willing to play their game before they push it to every device in the world - that's where soft launch comes in. Available in just a handful of countries and regions, a soft-launched game is subject to drastic change as developers take on board customer feedback (and other metrics) to alter the game and ensure the best possible product is ready for when it goes to worldwide launch.

Industry observers note that but here's the kicker - we can see when developers do that. And when you're looking at some of the massive games, like the ones we have on this list, then you can find yourself getting very excited, and even a little jealous that you can't play them yet.

So to help you out a little, we've collected a huge list of some of the biggest and best games right now available in soft launch, which you might well be able to get if you have the right Apple ID or Google Play account to download them with.

It has been revealed that just as a note: In the case of a game suddenly disappearing, it might be because the developer has decided to stop development on it early and save themselves the cost of a big launch, or because the developer is gearing up for a big launch and wants to surprise the world. Whatever the case, we'll try to keep you updated when these things happen.

Recent findings suggest that let's get into the list! SoulTerra Odyssey.

An interesting one here. Bandai Namco has dived back into the mobile world with a completely new IP. They're also claiming it's the first 'Match3D Roguelite Battle Game ever.' Given the sheer breadth of games out there, I highly doubt it, but it's an intriguing combination, nonetheless.

Sonic Rumble sees the blue blur returning to mobile, this time as a battle royale of sorts. In the mould of games like Stumble Guys and Fall Guys, it appears we can expect to dash around obstacle-filled courses, dodging the numerous hazards that threaten to eliminate us at every turn. It's definitely a setup that suits Sonic and co, but is it entering a market that's already been conquered by Scopely? Only time will tell.

Sources indicate that casual strategy games are all the rage these days, particularly on mobile. Anything that gives you a slight hit of feeling clever without requiring in-depth tactics that take forever to learn. Century Games' Crown of Bones is the latest attempt at sliding into that niche. It sees you joining the Skeleton King and his army as they battle through numerous realms. It sports a colourful art style that reminds me somewhat of little toy towns and villages, something you might have created in real life as a child, perhaps. As for the gameplay, it pretty much consists of increasing your numbers, upgrading your troops and toppling your opponents. There are a few special items thrown in for good measure as well.

If you're a football fan, you're probably already aware of Nordeus as the folks behind the popular management sim Top Eleven. With their latest effort, Top Goal, they are swapping the touchline for the pitch as you take direct control over your squad, having a more active role in the outcome of a match. Still, it seems some of the strategic side remains as you build your squad and choose your formation before taking on other players in PvP.

While it might seem as though the era of endless runners has passed on mobile, several still do very well, particularly if they have brand power behind them. Zapak hopes that Ben 10 Alien Run can join that list, putting a lot of stock in the popular children's cartoon pulling in the younger generation.

In it, you will dash around while transforming into one of nine different aliens, each bringing special abilities to the table. That might be creating a shield to block an enemy attack in one instance, while another might clear the path ahead with laser beams. On top of that, there are the usual daily challenges and missions you'd expect from the genre.

Sources indicate that oh My Anne is a match-3 game based on the popular novel series Anne of Green Gables. Players proceed through the story by completing levels and associated challenges. It's certainly interesting to see Neowiz deciding to take established, historical (1908~) novels and their IP and spin them off into games. There's a question to be asked about brand recognition and 'crossover IP' when those IPs are not ones from the current vogue. We regularly see Warhammer and Marvel crossover games, but those things are currently 'in', Anne of Green Gables — and Oh My Anne — targets a different audience and plays by different rules of advertising. Could there be a Dracula, Canterbury Tales or Beowulf games on the horizon if this takes off?

NetEase's Stumble Guys killer, Eggy Party, is rapidly moving toward its global release with seven new regions granted access to it in January of 2024; before that, it was simply in the SEA region. What's the significant appeal? Well, if you're not sold by the constant party, cheerful colours and multiplayer mania of Eggy Party, then maybe the map creation will be the thing to grab your attention. A bumbling race to the finish might be fun, but doing it on a map that you - or one of your friends - created is vastly more fun.

Zynga, who you likely know for, well, many things, are working on a upcoming addition to their growing merge catalogue. FruitFall – don't forget the double capital Fs – tasks you with merging fruits to beat each level. Simple, right? Judging by the store description, expect this to become more difficult as you progress. At first, it'll likely be a case of simply merging fruit, while the latter stages will introduce troublesome crates and frozen fruit that need thawing out before becoming useful. Zynga claims each level brings something different, keeping the challenge fresh and fun. Time will tell if that's the case.

Recent findings suggest that mattel Match: Toybox looks to bring together the company's many toys under one roof, including Uno, Masters of the Universe and, of course, Barbie. How? You might ask. Through match-3 puzzling, that's how.

As you'll likely have guessed from the name, Puzzletown Mysteries sees you unravel mysteries by solving puzzles. There is also a town involved. The overarching whodunit is whether poor Gladys slipped from her balcony or if she received a little push before toppling over the edge, while you'll also look into a case of stolen cats.

As you've likely already guessed from the name, we're talking tower defence here. Here, the slight twist on the usual formula is that, alongside setting up your various defences, you'll actually build the map your enemies will march down. Of course, that's something we've seen before, but it's a fun twist nevertheless. I'm quite fond of the visuals, which have a super clean and easy-to-read look that's just shy of qualifying as minimalist.

Diamond Dreams is looking to bring a sense of elegance to the match-3 genre. The whole idea is that you're working towards crafting some stunning jewellery that, I have to say, looks far better than it possibly needs to.

Given the immense popularity of Monopoly Go, it seemed inevitable that similar games would pop up eventually. Coin Master – Board Adventure from Moon Active is one such attempt. Having already achieved success with Coin Master, I'd imagine this will also do incredibly well.

Sources indicate that cats & Soup has made a name for itself in recent times with its lovely aesthetic and focus on feline companions. While it's still a fairly familiar idle RPG, the focus on cosiness helped it stand out from a massive crowd. Evidently buoyed by its success, a spin-off called Cats & Soup: Magic Recipe is now in the works. Once again, the team are taking on a familiar mobile genre, bringing some warm-fuzzy cuteness to the merge-and-match realm. The aim is to cook delicious recipes, build a lovely home for your kitties, and make friends with new cats.

Recent findings suggest that the humble match-3 will likely never lose popularity on mobile. It's simple to understand and great for playing on the go since it hits a nice spot between relaxing and engaging the brain. It's not surprising, then, that we often have big franchises delve into the genre. The latest to try their white-gloved hand is Disney with Disney Magic Match 3D. In it, you'll remove colourful clutter. No, really. Check out Catherine's preview to learn more.

In a recent development, while George R R Martin might have no interest in finishing his own book series, there is still plenty of Game of Thrones content to enjoy. Dragonfire is the latest, a tile-based strategy game that lets you put the titular fire-breathing winged beasties to work. But it's not simply sending them into battle. You will hatch and train them, taking your little fiery friend from a cute baby to a creature capable of barbecuing enemy villages.

Recent findings suggest that we all love Fruit Ninja, but if there's one criticism you can throw its way, it's that it didn't have much else going for it beyond slicing up fruit. Adventure looks to change this by introducing a level-based approach that sees you solving puzzles alongside stabbing melons. You can also unlock latest weapons and abilities as you progress, presumably allowing you to dice a kiwi in untold ways.

Recent findings suggest that fairyTale Quest is a roguelite action RPG in the style of something like Vampire Survivors. And its characters? Well, as you've likely guessed, they're all pulled from traditional stories. So you can expect the Substantial Bad Wolf and Red Riding Hood to fight by your side. They can put aside their differences for the greater good, it seems.

That's right. Plants Vs Zombies 3 is back in soft launch, this time with Evolved after the colon. This refers to the merging mechanics they're throwing in with their latest attempt. We'll see how that all pans out in due course, but it's hard not to be a little sceptical given that EA has clearly struggled to figure out what they want to do with PvZ.

It has been revealed that it's been almost ten years since Hill Climb Racing 2 rolled out, so it likely feels about time for a sequel for fans of wacky, physics-based driving. In the third instalment, you can expect plenty of special gadgets and handy boosts for increasing your performance on the bouncy track. There are also the plentiful customisation options on offer that any self-respecting racer needs. If we can't pimp our ride, what's the point?

Aside from the obvious flock and little green candy-loving monster, there are few games more iconic on mobile than Temple Run. That's why the announcement of a third has got us excited here at Pocket Gamer. But do those simple yet effective mechanics stand up after all these years, or are massive changes needed? Well, check out Catherine's Temple Run 3 preview to see what she thought.

It has been revealed that cute little penguins running around an obstacle course in Fall/Stumble Guys fashion? Haven't we already seen this with Pudgy Party? Apparently, Smilegate thinks they can do better, and personally, I'm all for it. Penguins are wonderful little creatures, and the more games where they're the star, the better. It sees you participating in 10-minute matches where the aim is to get your beak across the line first.

Industry observers note that if you love pinging marbles and cutesy creatures, Marblebound might be the perfect fit for you. You gather a team of four heroes and then head into battle to take down a series of fearsome foes. And you'll do that by firing marbles at them, including ricocheting them off walls if you know your angles.

FunPlus, who you may know from State of Survival and DC: Dark Legion, among others, appears to be working on a latest game. This one's called Dark Shot Survival and sees you building up a base to fend off night creatures (yes, they look like zombies to me, too). The whole thing seems to centre around a day/night cycle, wherein you spend the waking hours gathering resources and fortifying your base. Then, when the sun goes down, you'll need to fend off the zomb— sorry, night creatures, with all your might.

Recent findings suggest that angry Birds Rush sees Rovio's recognisable avians slinging themselves into a different genre. By the looks of things, Rush is an endless runner that sees you bouncing through various colourful locales all inspired by the series' many other games. It doesn't appear to be a straightforward runner, though, with slingshot elements still present to some extent.

In a recent development, there are few cartoon duos more iconic than Tom & Jerry. I'm not even a huge fan of them, but they'd certainly spring to mind if I had to name two long-standing cartoon rivals. It's that instant recognition that probably helped Steer Studios decide it was an IP worth working with. Tom and Jerry Blast is a puzzler that, based on the screenshots, sees you tapping your way through each level and using boosters if they ever become overly tricky.

Recent findings suggest that you wouldn't necessarily put sailing the seven seas and tower defence together, but that's exactly what Puzala is going for with Stormborn Era. In it, you take charge of Black Sam and his crew, defending their ship from the hordes of enemies that have nothing better to do with their time than attack a major boat.

The Girls' Frontline series has proven incredibly popular over the years. Apparently, conventionally attractive women with guns will always do well. Who knew? Anyway, you can check out Catherine's Ahead of the Game to see if it's more than just a surface-level shooter.

Industry observers note that having briefly appeared in the US a while back, Borderlands Mobile has crept back into soft launch in Canada. The latest iteration has revealed that we can play as long-time fan-favourite Mad Moxxi, which I'm sure will be welcome news to many folks.

VW’s ID.Polo GTI Clubsport Concept Is a Track-Focused EV

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (465 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Volkswagen GTI badge has been a staple in automotive culture for 50 years, and it’s clearly not getting sidelined anytime soon.
  • In a recent development, while it’s not heading to production, the Clubsport concept is a peek into the possibilities riding on the electric ID.Polo GTI, which became the first EV to wear the GTI badge when it was released earlier this year.
  • See all results for Volkswagen ID.GTI for sale near 92604.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Volkswagen GTI badge has been a staple in automotive culture for 50 years, and it’s clearly not getting sidelined anytime soon. VW just released the ID.Polo GTI Clubsport concept, an electric track-focused GTI that slots in as the automaker’s fourth latest GTI variant this year.

In a recent development, while it’s not heading to production, the Clubsport concept is a peek into the possibilities riding on the electric ID.Polo GTI, which became the first EV to wear the GTI badge when it was released earlier this year. The standard ID.Polo GTI, which isn’t sold in the United States, reaches 62 mph in 6.8 seconds thanks to a 223-hp electric motor mounted to the front axle.

See all results for Volkswagen ID.GTI for sale near 92604.

The Clubsport concept ups the ante, with VW claiming it will hit 62 mph in just 4.7 seconds with the help of launch control and a more powerful APP550 electric motor. The upgraded motor, which is typically used to power the rear wheels of larger models like the ID.Tiguan and ID.7, sends 362 horsepower to the front wheels and nearly doubles the standard electric GTI’s torque output from 213 to 406 pound-feet.

Industry observers note that volkswagen also equipped the concept vehicle with an electronically regulated front differential lock, a performance-tuned adaptive suspension system, and ceramic brakes with a one-box brake setup. The high-performance powertrain fits into an equally aggressive two-door build, complete with a large front splitter, diffuser, and a flared rear wing.

Rather than the typical five-seater setup, the Clubsport concept houses two Recaro bucket seats with red five-point harnesses. A Tornado Red roll bar replaces the rear seats, and the cockpit is solely reserved for racing needs, meaning the standard infotainment system is also omitted. The cabin is finished in a dark microfiber material and trimmed with red stitching.

Volkswagen calls this concept the “perfect match of heritage and future,” and the automaker claims its young employees were involved in much of the concept’s realization. The ID.Polo GTI Clubsport concept won’t ever make it to VW showrooms, but it’ll be displayed next week at the Essen Motor Show in Essen, Germany.

Alayna Wilkening grew up reading motorsport magazines and following her grandpa around his Chevrolet dealership's showroom floor. In true Hoosier fashion, her first car was a hot pink custom cardboard "Fiero-vette" for her kindergarten Kindy 500 race. She now autocrosses a 1994 Miata with her dad, which she learned to drive the night before her first event. Alayna went to Indiana University and graduated with a degree in journalism and a minor in graphic design. As a testament to her great taste in cars, her first real one was a metallic orange 2007 Chevy HHR, which she lovingly called "The Dumptruck.".

Breaking: Scientists create a remarkable new rechargeable battery using vitamin B12

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (965 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that scientists have found an unexpected fresh use for vitamin B12, a nutrient best known for its importance to human health.
  • Vitamin B12 is essential for normal bodily function and is naturally present in animal products.
  • According to recent reports, now, scientists are exploring an entirely different application.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that scientists have found an unexpected fresh use for vitamin B12, a nutrient best known for its importance to human health. Researchers at the University of Córdoba have incorporated the vitamin into a rechargeable battery, demonstrating for the first time that it can serve as a catalyst in this type of energy storage system.

Vitamin B12 is essential for normal bodily function and is naturally present in animal products. The vitamin is produced by certain bacteria, which occur in nature and are also grown commercially to supply the food and pharmaceutical industries. In addition to its established applications in medicine, nutrition, and veterinary care, B12 is used to address certain nutritional deficiencies. It has also become popular alongside other B vitamins as a hangover remedy because of its potential to help reduce fatigue.

According to recent reports, now, scientists are exploring an entirely different application. By using the vitamin to support the chemical reactions inside a battery, they have developed a prototype capable of completing up to 250 charging and discharging cycles.

How Vitamin B12 Makes a Rechargeable Battery Possible.

Recent findings suggest that the new battery was developed by the Physical Chemistry research group (FQM-204) at the University of Córdoba's Chemical Institute for Energy and the Environment (IQUEMA). It uses zinc and oxygen from the surrounding air to produce electricity, with vitamin B12, also called cobalamin, playing a crucial role in the process.

To make the design work, the researchers attached vitamin B12 molecules to single-walled carbon nanotubes. The vitamin contains cobalt (III) at its center, which helps drive the electrochemical reactions needed for the battery to function.

Sources indicate that the team has previously experimented with natural molecules as battery catalysts, including hemoglobin and catalase. These substances contain iron (II) and iron (III), respectively. Vitamin B12 represents the group's third effort to use a biological molecule for this purpose, but it has delivered an important advance: a battery that can be recharged repeatedly, completing as many as 250 cycles.

One of the biggest obstacles was keeping vitamin B12 inside the battery. Because the vitamin dissolves readily in water, it would normally be difficult to retain in a system that relies on a water-based electrolyte.

The researchers overcame this problem by securing the vitamin to carbon nanotubes, using an approach inspired by how amino acids connect to form proteins.

Manuel Cano Luna, one of the study's authors, explained that "we looked at the properties we can find in naturally occurring materials to use them in new batteries," while describing the team's search for useful biological compounds.

Their attachment technique imitates "the process by which amino acids bind together in proteins.".

Alongside Cano Luna, the research team included Valentín García Caballero, Miguel López León, Pablo Gómez Argudo, Luis Camacho Delgado, José Miguel Rodríguez Mellado, María Teresa Martín Romero, José Abad López, and Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero.

A Safer, Lighter Alternative to Lithium-Ion Batteries.

The findings, published in the Journal of Materials Chemistry A, could contribute to the development of battery technologies that depend less on the materials used in conventional lithium-ion batteries.

Although lithium-ion batteries are widely used, obtaining their raw materials can involve significant economic, environmental, and social challenges. Zinc-air batteries offer a potential alternative because they can store substantial amounts of energy relative to their weight while relying on materials that are more readily available.

In a recent development, zinc is abundant and recyclable, and these batteries use oxygen from the surrounding atmosphere as part of their energy-producing reactions. Because they draw oxygen from the air rather than storing all the necessary reactants internally, they can also be lighter than other battery designs.

This advantage has helped make zinc-air batteries increasingly useful in compact electronic devices, particularly hearing aids. Another benefit is their use of non-flammable, water-based electrolytes, which can reduce fire risks and improve safety.

Why Vitamin B12 Is Key to Recharging.

A major challenge in developing rechargeable zinc-air batteries is finding a catalyst that can efficiently support the chemical reactions involved in both producing and storing electricity.

During discharge, the battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy. Recharging requires the relevant chemical reactions to proceed in the opposite direction. A suitable catalyst must therefore be effective in both processes.

According to researcher Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero, vitamin B12 "has proven to meet the necessary conditions to act as a good catalyst because, during discharge, it catalyzes the reduction of oxygen to water and, during recharging, it promotes the production of oxygen.".

This ability to support both reactions is what makes the vitamin particularly promising for rechargeable zinc-air battery technology.

Could Vitamin B12 Help Store Renewable Energy?

The successful prototype offers a new direction for researchers seeking affordable, sustainable alternatives to existing energy storage technologies.

If the approach can be developed further, batteries using vitamin B12 catalysts could eventually help address one of the biggest challenges facing renewable energy: storing excess electricity generated by sources such as solar and wind power for use when production falls.

Recent findings suggest that although the technology remains at the research stage, demonstrating up to 250 charge and discharge cycles shows that a familiar biological molecule can play an unexpected role in rechargeable battery design. The discovery adds to growing efforts to use naturally occurring substances to create safer, lighter, and more sustainable ways to store energy.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season revision not intended to change the game significantly.
  • However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.
  • According to recent reports, the December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the new year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season revision not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

According to recent reports, the December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the new year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

It has been revealed that battlefield Studios announced a host of latest changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

Recent findings suggest that all tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

The focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an problem that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

The patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios claims should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

It has been revealed that going forward, Battlefield Studios said to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

It has been revealed that some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect fresh maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

  • According to recent reports, both versions come with an optional removable roof, which is pretty awesome.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Slate made a major splash with its affordable, heavily customizable electric truck. Someone even copied the formula over to a lineup of gas-powered trucks, and we'll see another cheap electric truck from Ford next year. But now the French have their own cheap electric truck concept. It's called the Kilow La Bagnole (which literally translates to "the car"), and it's adorable. I need one.

The La Bagnole is one of the most interesting looking cars I've ever seen, It looks like a French Willy's Jeep but with the fully open wheels of F1 car. It only seats two and two different kinds of body styles, Hard Top (basically a pickup truck) and Closed Hard Top (becomes a van). Both can be had with roof bars so you can put all sorts of gear up there. If you get the Hard Top, the side bed rails are made from either resin-bonded wood fiber or Okoume wood. The former makes it look like it's from IKEA, while the latter looks more premium. However, the Okoume wood requires periodic to keep it weather proof.

According to recent reports, both versions come with an optional removable roof, which is pretty awesome. So you can have either a targa-top pickup or van. The standard La Bagnole lacks doors, and only has significant metal side bars, but you can option transparent doors, which are neat.

If you want colors, boy can you get 'em. Kilow offers 12 different regular color options, six gradient colors, and six sparkly "Memories" colors. The best part is that they're all free options. The chassis of the La Bagnole is steel, but all of its body panels are easy removable. So if one breaks or dents, you can just replace it.

There are a few different battery options. Two of the options are made to allow unlicensed drivers to use them. Both the 6 kWh and 12 kWh "Long Range" batteries require no license, as they're classified as quadricycles and capped at 45 km/h (28 mph). Trucks with the 6 kWh battery have only 70 km (43 miles) of range. Cars with the 12 kWh battery can go 164 km (102 miles). The third option mates the 12 kWh battery with an increased speed limiter of 80 km/h (50 mph), but that requires a driver's license.

In a recent development, I love this little thing, and I wish it was coming to the United States. As of right now, it will only be offered in Europe, starting in France. The La Bagnole is such a charming, fun looking little utility vehicle that seems designed equally for function and form. With prices ranging from €10,800 ($11,758) - €13,690 ($14,904), it's an affordable work vehicle for anyone who needs one and stays local, but with tons of character.
